# Known bugs and defects in upstream code

Tracker for defects found by the 2026-09-24 code survey (19 subsystem readers, each adversarially verified) and re-verified item by item against the tree at `22c9c89c`. On 2026-09-25 every entry was checked again from the owner's local clone, this time with vanilla, Forge, NEI, AE2 and OpenComputers behaviour settled by `javap` on the dependency jars (the cloud survey could not read them); each correction was confirmed by two independent reviewers. That pass rewrote the entries whose description, location, severity or fix was wrong, moved the entries that turned out not to be defects to "Reviewed and rejected" (their IDs are not reused), and added 87 newly found defects (IDs from B-331 up to B-417). On 2026-09-26 the owner's mod pack was inspected (addon bytecode, mixins, configs, logs; `docs/fork-notes.md`, "Owner's play environment"): entries whose behaviour differs there, is live or moot under the owner's settings, or is constrained by an addon patch got a Note saying so, and 11 defects found in the process were added (B-418 to B-428). 417 entries are tracked. Line numbers are from the `22c9c89c` snapshot, which is still the state of `src/` apart from the fork version identity of 2026-09-26 (new `com/hbm/dbs/DBSVersion.java`, `HTTPHandler.loadStats`/`loadVersion` rewritten, three `ModEventHandler` lines replaced one for one, so its line numbers are unchanged); class and method names are the stable anchors. Everything here is upstream (HbmMods / NTM: Space) code. Each entry's `Plan:` line names its phase or decision row in `docs/fix-roadmap.md`.

How to use: pick from "Fix in the fork" first; each item there is safe to change without altering balance, saves or anything players notice. "Needs a decision" items change something players can notice (or existing worlds); decide per item and record it. Update the **Status** field when acting: `open`, `fixed <commit>` (the fix carries a `// DBS fix B-xxx` marker), `fixed <commit> (no-marker)` (assets, deletions and files outside `src/`, which cannot carry a marker), `fixed upstream <hash>` (a ported HbmMods fix; no marker), `wontfix <why>`. Any file may be edited to fix a defect (edit policy of 2026-09-25 in `CLAUDE.md`); every fix is compiled and tested locally before it reaches `space-travel-twopointfive` (a local session runs `./gradlew --offline compileJava` before hand-off and the owner tests on client and dedicated server; a cloud session commits untested to its `claude/...` staging branch).

Severity: **crash** (exception or hang reachable in normal play) · **save data** (NBT/persistence wrong) · **gameplay** (wrong behaviour players can hit) · **silent misconfig** (config or registration silently ignored) · **leak / perf** · **dead code** (misleading leftovers, unreachable features).

## Details by area

### Bootstrap, config, commands (`core`)

- **B-001** · crash · needs a decision · `src/main/java/com/hbm/handler/BlockMigrations.java:43`
  - BlockMigrations.doMigraion loops y upward from the height value (infinite loop). The empty migration body iterates `for(y = heightValue; y >= 0; y++)`, so if it were ever invoked it would spin forever (y only stops at int overflow). Currently unreachable because of the -1 stamp bug, so the two defects mask each other.
  - Evidence: `for(int y = chunk.getHeightValue(x, z); y >= 0; y++) { }`
  - Fix: Change to y-- (and add a body) before ever wiring buildNumber() in.
  - Plan: decision D1
  - Status: open
- **B-002** · crash · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/potion/HbmPotion.java:84-104`
  - HbmPotion.registerPotion sizes potionTypes to max(256, id), swallows errors and accepts ids above 127. The 8.xx potion id keys are unbounded ints (PotionConfig.java:33-48, defaults 62-77). An id >= 256 overflows the resized array by one (`new Potion[Math.max(256, id)]` cannot hold index id), and a failed reflective resize is swallowed by the empty catch and leaves the 32-slot vanilla array; either way the Potion constructor throws AIOOBE immediately at L104 (`new HbmPotion`), not later. Ids 128-255 register but are broken in play: vanilla carries the id as a signed byte in S1DPacketEntityEffect and in PotionEffect NBT, so the client gets a negative id (AIOOBE in PotionEffect.onUpdate) and the effect is dropped on reload.
  - Evidence: `Potion[] newArray = new Potion[Math.max(256, id)]; ... } catch (Exception e) { }` (L86, L99-101). javap: Potion.<init>(int,boolean,int) does `getstatic potionTypes; iload_1; aload_0; aastore`; PotionEffect.writeCustomPotionEffectToNBT does i2b + setByte("Id") and readCustomPotionEffectFromNBT returns null for a negative byte; the S1DPacketEntityEffect constructor stores `getPotionID() & 255` in a byte field; NetHandlerPlayClient.handleEntityEffect builds the PotionEffect from that sign-extended byte and PotionEffect.onUpdate indexes potionTypes[potionID].
  - Fix: In registerPotion reject any configured id outside 0..127 (vanilla packets and NBT carry a signed byte): throw with a message naming the 8.xx config key, or log via MainRegistry.logger.error and fall back to the default id. Keep the resize at 256 (every valid id then fits). Replace the empty catch with MainRegistry.logger.error("[Potion] could not resize Potion.potionTypes", e). Optionally warn when potionTypes[id] is already taken: a collision with a vanilla id (1-23) or another mod's potion silently overwrites it.
  - Note: In the owner's pack (found 2026-09-26) EndlessIDs 1.7.4 (extendPotion=true) resizes Potion.potionTypes to 65536 and carries ids above 127 as an int ('IdExtended' in NBT, an extra int in S1DPacketEntityEffect), while hodgepodge masks every PotionEffect id with & 255, so there ids 128-255 work, ids of 256 and up register without error but are silently remapped to id & 255, the resize branch (L84-102) never runs, and AntiIDConflict's crashIfConflict=true turns an id collision into a crash. Keep the portable fix (reject ids outside 0..127 by default; at most allow 128-255 when both endlessids and hodgepodge are loaded, never 256 or more); the fork potion band 110-119 (adopted 2026-09-26) is free in that pack.
  - Plan: Phase 2
  - Status: open
- **B-003** · save data · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/extprop/HbmLivingProps.java:496-498`
  - ContaminationEffect.load reads time/maxTime/ignoreArmor from the parent compound. load() fetches the child compound `me` but reads maxTime, time and ignoreArmor from the parent `nbt`, so every contamination effect restored from NBT (loadNBTData L442-445) comes back with maxTime=0/time=0/ignoreArmor=false; getRad() yields NaN and the effect is dead after a relog.
  - Evidence: `int maxTime = nbt.getInteger("maxTime"); int time = nbt.getInteger("time"); boolean ignoreArmor = nbt.getBoolean("ignoreArmor");`
  - Fix: Read all three fields from `me` (the child compound), matching save().
  - Plan: Phase 2
  - Status: open
- **B-004** · gameplay · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/main/MainRegistry.java:367-377`
  - ForgeChunkManager callback returns after the first NORMAL ticket. ticketsLoaded `return`s inside the loop once the NORMAL ticket is handled (L369-372), so ENTITY tickets listed after it never reach IChunkLoader.init(ticket); Forge neither saves nor re-forces a ticket's chunk list, so that call is what re-forces the entity's real chunk. The affected entities (EntityMissileBaseNT/EntityMissileCustom, EntityMissileAntiBallistic, EntityPlaneBase, EntityArtilleryShell, EntityArtilleryRocket, EntityBulletBaseMK4CL and the EntityExplosionChunkloading subclasses) already took a fresh ENTITY ticket in entityInit(), but Entity(World) runs entityInit before the chunk sets chunkCoordX/Z, so that ticket forced chunk (0,0) instead; after a world load they sit in an un-forced chunk and stall until a player comes near. Block chunkloaders and EntityDeliveryDrone are unaffected (see Evidence).
  - Evidence: `if(ticket.getType() == ForgeChunkManager.Type.NORMAL) { ChunkLoaderManager.loadTicket(world, ticket); return; }`. ChunkLoaderManager.java:43-48 requests a NORMAL ticket only when savedData.ticket == null (one per world) and loadTicket (L23-28) forces every chunksForcedBy entry on it; BlockTransporterRocket (L53, L60) is its only user. entityInit calls init(requestTicket(...ENTITY)) at EntityMissileBaseNT:102, EntityMissileAntiBallistic:46, EntityPlaneBase:72, EntityArtilleryShell:61, EntityArtilleryRocket:51, EntityBulletBaseMK4CL:34, EntityExplosionChunkloading:23; each init() keeps the first ticket and calls forceChunk(chunkCoordX, chunkCoordZ) (e.g. EntityMissileBaseNT:310-325, EntityExplosionChunkloading:27-36). EntityDeliveryDrone requests its ticket from readEntityFromNBT (L132 -> setChunkLoading L68-71), when posX/posZ are already set, and its init() re-forces from its position via loadNeighboringChunks (L195-207, L223-232). javap: Entity(World) sets worldObj at bc 110, calls entityInit at bc 174 and never writes chunkCoordX (Chunk.addEntity does); ForgeChunkManager.loadWorld loads the entity chunks, putAll's the tickets (bc 911) and then calls ticketsLoaded (bc 925); saveWorld stores only Type, ChunkListDepth, ModData, chunkX/chunkZ and the PersistentID.
  - Fix: Replace `return` with `continue` so every ticket in the list is processed; every init() keeps an existing loaderTicket and re-forces the now-correct chunkCoordX/Z. The construction-time (0,0) force and the unadopted persisted ticket are tracked separately: B-185 for the EntityExplosionChunkloading subclasses, and "Moving IChunkLoader entities force chunk (0,0) from entityInit and never adopt restored tickets" for the others.
  - Plan: Phase 6
  - Status: open
- **B-005** · gameplay · needs a decision · `src/main/java/com/hbm/main/ModEventHandler.java:1664-1670`
  - onPlayerClone drops NBT-only player props on death. The handler copies only the serialize() subset (shield, maxShield, backpack, HUD, reputation, ladder, magnet; HbmPlayerProps.java:203-222) and never checks event.wasDeath, so on death the new HbmPlayerProps loses hasWarped (in a WorldTypeTeleport world the player is warped again on the next login, ModEventHandler.java:237-244) and nitanCount (used by ItemFlask, ItemLemon and HbmPotion:190). maskManTimer and lastDimension are lost too, harmlessly: radiation (HbmLivingProps) is not carried over either, so BossSpawnHandler.java:91-92 zeroes the timer anyway at the default maskmanMinRad=50, and lastDimension is rewritten on every Nether entry (L1408-1411); the dash fields are never persisted and reset on every relog regardless. On End-portal return nothing is lost: Forge's EntityPlayer.clonePlayer(old, true) hands the new player the old extendedProperties map, so the handler serialises and deserialises the same object.
  - Evidence: `HbmPlayerProps.getData(event.original).serialize(buf); HbmPlayerProps.getData(event.entityPlayer).deserialize(buf);` saveNBTData (HbmPlayerProps.java:227-244) additionally holds nitan, hasWarped, lastDimension and maskManTimer. javap EntityPlayer.clonePlayer(EntityPlayer, boolean): when the flag is true, `this.extendedProperties = old.extendedProperties` followed by init(this, worldObj) on each entry (bc 71-124); Clone is posted with wasDeath = !flag, and ServerConfigurationManager.respawnPlayer passes its conqueredEnd argument as that flag.
  - Fix: Act only when event.wasDeath and copy the fields that should survive (at least hasWarped; decide nitanCount), e.g. a saveNBTData/loadNBTData round trip followed by resetting the fields meant to reset; do nothing when !wasDeath. The stale `props.player` after an End return is a separate entry (HbmPlayerProps.init is empty).
  - Plan: decision D2
  - Status: open
- **B-006** · silent misconfig · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/config/FalloutConfigJSON.java:292`
  - FalloutConfigJSON reads matchesMaterial from the mustBeOpaque key. readEntry checks obj.has("matchesMaterial") but then reads obj.get("mustBeOpaque").getAsString(). If mustBeOpaque is absent, which is true of every material entry in the generated _hbmFallout.json template, this NPEs, readConfig's catch-all returns null and initialize() keeps the defaults, so the whole custom hbmFallout.json is silently ignored (only a stack trace is printed). If mustBeOpaque is present, matNames.get("true"/"false") yields null and the entry loses its material restriction, so it matches every material instead of never matching.
  - Evidence: `if(obj.has("matchesMaterial")) entry.mMa(matNames.get(obj.get("mustBeOpaque").getAsString()));` write() (L260-281) emits mustBeOpaque only when matchesOpaque is true and matchesMaterial whenever the material is in matNames; no default calls mO (only clone() L186 and readEntry L291 do), while the mMa defaults (L68-72 wood/leaves/plants/vine, L98-102 iron/rock/sand/ground/grass) all emit matchesMaterial. readConfig (L145-162) catches everything and returns null; initialize (L45-50) then keeps the defaults; eval (L214) skips the material check when matchesMaterial is null.
  - Fix: Read obj.get("matchesMaterial").getAsString() instead of "mustBeOpaque"; optionally log an unknown material name instead of silently storing null.
  - Plan: Phase 6
  - Status: open
- **B-007** · dead code · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/config/GeneralConfig.java:28,31,118,121`
  - GeneralConfig enableVirus and enableSilentCompStackErrors field defaults contradict their config defaults. The static initialisers say true (L28, L31) but the hbm.cfg defaults are false (L118, L121). Nothing can observe the difference: the only readers (CrystalVirus.java:26, a block tick; RecipesCommon.java:102,182,192) run after PreLoad's loadConfig (MainRegistry.java:275), and a config read failure cannot surface the initialiser either, so this is a cosmetic inconsistency.
  - Evidence: `public static boolean enableVirus = true; ... config.get(CATEGORY_GENERAL, "1.21_enableVirus", false, ...).getBoolean(false);` and `public static boolean enableSilentCompStackErrors = true;` vs `"1.28_enableSilentCompStackErrors", false`. javap Configuration.load catches only IOException, after which get(...).getBoolean(false) returns the passed default; a corrupt file makes load() throw, and the Configuration(File) constructor used by loadConfig (MainRegistry.java:765) catches that, renames the file to *.errored and loads again (Forge Configuration.java:109-120), so the config default applies. A scan of com/hbm/config/*.java found no other initialiser/default mismatch.
  - Fix: Set both initialisers to their config defaults (enableVirus = false at L28, enableSilentCompStackErrors = false at L31).
  - Plan: Phase 7
  - Status: open
- **B-008** · silent misconfig · needs a decision · `src/main/java/com/hbm/handler/HTTPHandler.java:26-58`
  - HTTPHandler version check compares against JameH2's RefStrings on GitHub. loadVersion downloads RefStrings.java from JameH2/space-travel-twopointfive and sets newVersion when its VERSION differs. The fork has never changed RefStrings.VERSION, so a locally built jar reports a new version only when JameH2 commits a different string (whether it differs today cannot be checked offline), while a CI-built jar carries the build day's count, which practically never equals a committed string, so it reads outdated; the login MOTD (ModEventHandler.java:205-213) also shows the "JamesH2 & Mellow's NTM: Space" banner and links to JameH2's releases. loadVersion shares one try block with loadSoyuz/loadTips/loadSpaceTips (L26-33), so a failed version fetch silently skips the Soyuz and tip texts too.
  - Evidence: `new URL("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JameH2/Hbm-s-Nuclear-Tech-GIT/space-travel-twopointfive/..."); newVersion = !RefStrings.VERSION.equals(sub)` (L43-58). RefStrings.java:6 `VERSION = "1.0.27 BETA (5778)"`, last changed upstream (the fork's only commit touching the file, 27811a59, is the LF normalisation). .github/workflows/build.yml:48 seds VERSION to `"1.0.27 BETA ($days)"` in the runner, with `permissions: contents: read` and no commit step. ModEventHandler.java:204-220: MOTD gated by GeneralConfig.enableMOTD, link https://github.com/JameH2/Hbm-s-Nuclear-Tech-GIT/releases.
  - Fix: Either remove the check (skip loadVersion; newVersion stays false) or compare a fork-specific marker that CI does not rewrite (the CI sed replaces the whole VERSION string, so the marker cannot live inside VERSION, and pointing the URL at the fork's branch alone would flag every CI build). In both cases change or drop the banner and release link at ModEventHandler.java:205-213. Run loadVersion in its own try/catch so a failure (e.g. a 404 on a private or renamed fork repository) does not suppress loadSoyuz/loadTips/loadSpaceTips.
  - Note: D3 answered 2026-09-26 (owner: give the fork its own version and update check). - **B-017** · crash · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/api/hbm/fluidmk2/FluidNetMK2.java:45-48,59-62,75-79`
  - FluidNetMK2 indexes its 6-slot pressure arrays with unclamped pressures; reachable server crash. providers/fluidAvailable/fluidDemand/receivers are sized HIGHEST_VALID_PRESSURE+1 = 6 (L45-48) and setupFluidProviders/setupFluidReceivers index them with the raw pressure range (L59-62, L75-79), so a pressure outside 0..5 throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on the next update of a net that holds both a provider and a receiver entry (L33-34; a compressor piped to its own fluid type is both). Default content stays within 0..5, but two paths reach other values: a recipe JSON can give any fluid pressure, which the compressor, hydrotreater and ModuleMachineBase output tanks adopt, and `TileEntityMachineCompressorBase.receiveControl`/`pasteSettings` trust the `compression` value, so one crafted `NBTControlPacket` from any player within about 11 blocks sets output pressure 6 (compression=5) or input pressure -1 (compression=-1). The exception escapes `UniNodespace.updateNodespace` in the ServerTickEvent handler and crashes the server.
  - Evidence: `for(int i = 0; i < IFluidUserMK2.HIGHEST_VALID_PRESSURE + 1; i++) providers[i] = new ArrayList();` (L24); `providers[p].add(...)` at L61 and `receivers[p][priority].add(...)` at L78, with `p` taken from `getProvidingPressureRange`/`getReceivingPressureRange` (IFluidStandardSenderMK2.java:111-122, IFluidStandardReceiverMK2.java:50-62). JSON: `SerializableRecipe.readFluidStack` L406 `int pressure = array.size() < 3 ? 0 : array.get(2).getAsInt();`, adopted at TileEntityMachineCompressorBase.java:187/237/330, TileEntityMachineHydrotreater.java:105 and ModuleMachineBase.java:45 (`conform`). Packet: TileEntityMachineCompressorBase.java:227-235 `tanks[0].withPressure(compression)` / `tanks[1].withPressure(compression + 1)` (re-applied every tick by setupTanks L185; pasteSettings L318-335 is identical); GUICompressor.java:46-52 only sends 0..4; NBTControlPacket.java:85 checks only hasPermission, which is isUseableByPlayer, distance squared <= 128 (TileEntityMachineCompressorBase.java:221-222, TileEntityMachineBase.java:86-92). compression=5 gives providing range [5,6] and `providers[6]` throws at L61; compression=-1 gives receiving range [-1,0] and `receivers[-1]` throws at L78. `UniNodespace.updateNodespace` has no catch and runs from ModEventHandler.java:1558; FML `EventBus.post` calls handleException and then Throwables.propagate (javap). By contrast FluidPump.java:212 clamps its pressure to 0..5.
  - Fix: Clamp in setupFluidProviders/setupFluidReceivers as the crash guard (`for(int p = Math.max(0, r[0]); p <= Math.min(HIGHEST_VALID_PRESSURE, r[1]); p++)`). Also validate at the sources: clamp `compression` to 0..4 in TileEntityMachineCompressorBase.receiveControl and pasteSettings, and clamp the pressure in SerializableRecipe.readFluidStack to 0..HIGHEST_VALID_PRESSURE with a warning through MainRegistry.logger.
  - Plan: Phase 5
  - Status: open

- **B-027** · gameplay · needs a decision · `src/main/java/api/hbm/block/IToolable.java:26-45`
  - ToolType.getType does not recognise damaged tools and ignores register() after its first call. The lookup map is keyed by a full ComparableStack, whose hashCode/equals include meta and stack size, while the keys are built from `new ItemStack(this)` (meta 0), so a damageable tool stops being recognised once used: a used screwdriver no longer makes PneumoTube (L102) or PneumoTubePaintableBlock (L164) return false, nor a used hand drill or defuser PneumoTubePaintableBlock, so on a compressor or endpoint tube a non-sneaking right-click opens the GUI instead of running the tool's onScrew action, and the BlockToolConversion look overlay (L111, L148) disappears for damaged tools, the Archineer wrench included. Separately, the map is filled lazily on the first getType call and later calls short-circuit on !map.isEmpty(), so a register() after that is ignored; in-tree every register() runs in an item constructor during ModItems init, before any play-time lookup, and /ntmreload never touches ToolType, so this only affects an addon that registers late.
  - Evidence: `private static HashMap<ComparableStack, ToolType> map = new HashMap();` (L26); `if(!map.isEmpty()) { return map.get(new ComparableStack(stack)); }` (L34-36); ComparableStack.hashCode adds `meta` and `stacksize` and equals compares them (RecipesCommon.java:179-219). Registrations: `type.register(new ItemStack(this));` (ItemTooling.java:22), ItemBoltgun.java:35, ItemBlowtorch.java:35. Durability: defuser 100 (ModItems.java:4111), screwdriver 100 (L4177), hand_drill 100 (L4179), wrench_archineer 1000 (L4181); ItemTooling.onItemUse damages the stack (L33-34). ItemInWorldManager.activateBlockOrUseItem calls onBlockActivated before onItemUse unless the player sneaks with an item (javap).
  - Fix: Key the map by Item: `private static HashMap<Item, ToolType> map = new HashMap();`, fill it in register() (`stacksForDisplay.add(stack); map.put(stack.getItem(), this);`), look up with `return stack == null ? null : map.get(stack.getItem());`, and remove the lazy fill.
  - Plan: decision D34
  - Status: open

- **B-030** · leak / perf · needs a decision · `src/main/java/api/hbm/tile/ILoadedTile.java:20,33-48`
  - ILoadedTile.TileAccessCache is a static map with no World identity that is never evicted. Every trySubscribe/tryProvide lookup puts an entry keyed by (x,y,z,dim); entries are only replaced when a lookup at the same key finds them expired, invalid or unloaded, and nothing ever calls clear()/remove(), so the map grows with every position ever probed. MinecraftServer.stopServer does not unload chunks or invalidate TEs, so after a singleplayer world switch the cached TEs stay valid and isLoaded, keep the old WorldServer alive through TileEntity.worldObj, and are judged against the new world's total time: reopening the same save serves stale TEs for up to NONNULL_CACHE (60) ticks and cached nulls for up to NULL_CACHE (20), and opening a save with a lower total world time serves them at matching coordinates until that world's time passes the old expiresOn, so dead TEs absorb direct tryProvide transfers and cached nulls hide real neighbours (machines may fail to connect).
  - Evidence: `public static Map<Quartet, TileAccessCache> cache = new HashMap(); ... TileAccessCache.cache.put(publicCumRag.clone(), cache);`; hasExpired (L33-38) checks only isInvalid, `worldTime >= expiresOn` and isLoaded, and TileEntityLoadedBase clears isLoaded only in onChunkUnload (L38). javap: MinecraftServer.stopServer calls saveAllWorlds, then posts WorldEvent.Unload and flushes each world, then DimensionManager.setWorld(id, null), with no chunk unload; Minecraft.loadWorld(WorldClient, String) posts WorldEvent.Unload for the old WorldClient on the client thread.
  - Fix: Evict expired or invalid entries from a periodic server-thread pass (e.g. next to the UniNodespace reaper, updateReapTimer). On WorldEvent.Unload, only when `!event.world.isRemote`, remove the entries whose Quartet dimension is `event.world.provider.dimensionId` (stopServer posts this on the server thread for every world), as PollutionHandler.java:146 and ChunkRadiationHandlerNT.java:227 already guard; alternatively clear everything on FMLServerStoppedEvent. Never clear from a client-side event: the map is a plain HashMap used by the integrated-server thread. Coordinate with B-107 (UniNodespace.worlds has the same pinning).
  - Plan: Phase 5 after D6
  - Status: open

- **B-037** · gameplay · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/blocks/fluid/CoriumFluid.java:23-29`
  - CoriumFluid returns icons of never-instantiated CoriumBlock (null). Neither Forge nor NTM reads a Forge fluid's icons (Forge's RenderBlockFluid takes block icons and is null-safe), so only a third-party fluid renderer (a tank or pipe mod displaying corium_fluid) can hit the null; not a crash in normal play.

- **B-336** · gameplay · needs a decision · `src/main/java/com/hbm/blocks/generic/BlockHazard.java:27,120-146`
  - Radioactive BlockHazard blocks stop emitting chunk radiation after a restart. `rad` is a field of the Block singleton and is 0 after every start. Only onBlockAdded (L138-146) sets it from the hazard registry and schedules the first tick, and updateTick (L120-127) adds chunk radiation and reschedules itself only while rad > 0. Scheduled ticks are saved with the chunk (TileTicks) and fire again after loading. A block placed in an earlier session can therefore tick before any block of its type has been placed in the current session; it then sees rad == 0, does nothing and is never rescheduled, and stays inert until it is broken and placed again. BlockHazardFalling (BlockHazardFalling.java:17,40-66; block_yellowcake, block_red_phosphorus, block_fallout) repeats the pattern. The 32 BlockHazard-family blocks in ModBlocks (BlockHazard, BlockHotHazard, BlockNuclearWaste, BlockHazardFalling) include the uranium, thorium, plutonium, fuel, waste, corium, schrabidium, radium and fallout blocks. BlockSellafield avoids the problem: it sets rad in its constructor (BlockSellafield.java:41), ticks through random ticks (`needsRandomTick = true`, L40) instead of scheduled ones, and empties onBlockAdded (L66). Radiation carried by the items (HazardSystem) is unaffected.
  - Evidence: `protected float rad = 0.0F;` (L27); `rad = HazardSystem.getHazardLevelFromStack(new ItemStack(this), HazardRegistry.RADIATION) * 0.1F;` (L142, the only assignment); `if(this.rad > 0) { ChunkRadiationManager.proxy.incrementRad(world, x, y, z, rad); world.scheduleBlockUpdate(x, y, z, this, this.tickRate(world)); }` (L123-126). javap AnvilChunkLoader: writeChunkToNBT stores World.getPendingBlockUpdates under TileTicks and readChunkFromNBT re-schedules them through World.func_147446_b. None of the 32 ModBlocks entries (ModBlocks.java:1551-1637) calls setTickRandomly.
  - Fix: In both classes compute rad lazily through a helper used by updateTick and tickRate. The hazard registry is filled in PreLoad (MainRegistry.java:296-297), before any world ticks. The helper must not overwrite a rad set in a constructor, because BlockSellafield sets its own. This keeps blocks whose ticks are still pending radiating across restarts. Blocks that already went inert have no pending tick and recover only through setTickRandomly(true) (a random tick then calls updateTick, which reschedules) or a one-time re-arm.
  - Note: Re-arming changes existing worlds: storage and waste blocks that have been silent since a restart start emitting chunk radiation again.
  - Note: BlockNuclearWaste.updateTick (BlockNuclearWaste.java:14-23) vents radon and then calls super.updateTick, so waste blocks also stop venting radon once the chain ends.
  - Plan: decision D35
  - Status: open

- **B-049** · crash · needs a decision · `src/main/java/com/hbm/blocks/BlockDummyable.java:174`
  - BlockDummyable.positions/internalPlayers: unsynchronized per-Block scratch state. One Block instance serves the client and integrated-server threads: findCore clears the instance list `positions` (170, field 174) and findCoreRec checks and appends it (190, 201), so two concurrent walks over the same multiblock can make findCore return a spurious null (ThreeInts.equals compares by value, so the other walk's coordinates match at 190) or, rarely, throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException from a concurrent ArrayList.add; findCore itself cannot throw ConcurrentModificationException (no iterator is involved). Both threads reach findCore in singleplayer (addCollisionBoxesToList 505 and collisionRayTrace 549 on both sides, drawHighlight 587 client-side), and a spurious null means missing collision boxes, a GUI that does not open (456-457), or an NPE in getSettings (610-611) and infoForDisplay (629-630), which never null-check pos. internalPlayers (492) is iterated with for-each only on the server thread (91 in onNeighborBlockChange, 114 in updateTick) while the client thread can add to it from onBlockPlacedBy (290; the isRemote check is only at 280), which can throw ConcurrentModificationException; each walk is only a few steps, so the race window is small.
  - Evidence: `List<ThreeInts> positions = new ArrayList<>(); ... private List<EntityPlayer> internalPlayers = new ArrayList<>();`; BlockDummyable.java:170/190/201 (clear/contains/add, no iterator), 91/114 (for-each), 290 (add), 610-611 and 629-630 (pos dereferenced without a null check; pasteSettings 620-621 checks); handler/ThreeInts.java:28-43 (equals by value, null-safe). javap: World.markAndNotifyBlock calls notifyBlockChange only when !isRemote and World.scheduleBlockUpdate is empty in the base World, so onNeighborBlockChange/updateTick run server-side only; ItemBlock.placeBlockAt calls onBlockPlacedBy with no isRemote check.
  - Fix: Make `positions` a local Set passed through findCoreRec (no callers outside BlockDummyable: 171, 176, 203, so it compiles); make internalPlayers a ThreadLocal or a per-World map; null-check pos in getSettings (611) and infoForDisplay (630), as pasteSettings (621) does (shared with B-053).
  - Plan: decision D8
  - Status: open

  - Evidence: `public FluidTank water;` (TileEntityMachinePumpBase.java:54), `public long power;` (TileEntityMachinePumpElectric.java:12), `public FluidTank steam; public FluidTank lps;` (TileEntityMachinePumpSteam.java:11-12); the three files contain no readFromNBT/writeToNBT (grep NBT: no hits), and TileEntityLoadedBase.readFromNBT/writeToNBT (L55-67) store only muffled and tilted.
  - Fix: Add readFromNBT/writeToNBT to TileEntityMachinePumpBase (water, through FluidTank.readFromNBT/writeToNBT with a key, as TileEntityMachinePolluting does) and to the two subclasses (power; steam and lps), each calling super.

  - Status: open

- **B-347** · gameplay · needs a decision · `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/TileEntityMachinePolluting.java:48-59`
  - TileEntityMachinePolluting.pollute(FluidType, release, amount) ignores its amount. The FluidType overload passes each per-mB value of the fluid's FT_Polluting burn or release map straight to pollute(PollutionType, float) and never uses `amount`, whereas the static FT_Polluting.pollute multiplies by the mB released (FT_Polluting.java:96-106). The callers pass the burned volume: the diesel generator `5F` every 5 ticks for the 5 mB it burned (TileEntityMachineDiesel.java:267-272), the oil burner `toBurn * 5` (TileEntityHeaterOilburner.java:86-87), the combustion engine `toBurn * 0.5F` (TileEntityMachineCombustionEngine.java:99-100) and the turbofan `amountToBurn * 5` every 20 ticks (TileEntityMachineTurbofan.java:194). These machines therefore emit one mB's worth of smoke per call whatever their fuel use, while gas flares, tanks, drains and the blast furnace, which call FT_Polluting.pollute, scale with volume. This is a regression. The overload scaled by amount from `81a3c19e` ("Added smokestack support to fluid burning lads") onwards, until HbmMods `7532f57f` ("animationes", 2026-03-24) moved its tank handling into pollute(PollutionType, float) and dropped the factor.
  - Evidence: `for(Map.Entry<PollutionType, Float> entry : map.entrySet()) { pollute(entry.getKey(), entry.getValue()); }` (L56-58); before `7532f57f` the loop body was `int fluidAmount = (int) Math.ceil(entry.getValue() * amount * 100);` (git show 7532f57f -- TileEntityMachinePolluting.java); `PollutionHandler.incrementPollution(world, x, y, z, entry.getKey(), entry.getValue() * mB);` (FT_Polluting.java:104). The trait values are per mB, e.g. SOOT_REFINED_OIL = PollutionHandler.SOOT_PER_SECOND * 0.025F (Fluids.java:293) on DIESEL through P_FUEL (Fluids.java:306, 346).
  - Fix: `pollute(entry.getKey(), entry.getValue() * amount);` at L57, which restores the behaviour before `7532f57f`.
  - Note: Compared with today, diesel generators would emit 5x more soot per call, and the oil burner, combustion engine and turbofan would scale with burn rate, so their smoke tanks fill and overflow into chunk pollution (L40-46) much faster.

- **B-348** · leak / perf · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/machine/TileEntityMachineElectricFurnace.java:215-224`
  - Electric furnace re-sets its block on almost every server tick. `trigger` is false only on a tick where the furnace has power, can process and progress is 0, so updateBlockState runs on nearly every tick, idle or working, not only when the lit state changes. MachineElectricFurnace.updateBlockState (MachineElectricFurnace.java:153-172) calls world.setBlock(x, y, z, furnace_on or furnace_off), which is setBlock(..., 0, 3) with meta 0. The stored meta is the facing (2-5), so Chunk.func_150807_a treats the call as a change even when the block is the same. It runs breakBlock (keepInventory suppresses the drop), removes the tile entity, runs onBlockAdded (setDefaultDirection rewrites the meta, L67-100) and creates a fresh TileEntityMachineElectricFurnace. setBlockMetadataWithNotify then restores the facing and setTileEntity puts the old tile back. Every placed electric furnace therefore does the following 20 times a second: it constructs and discards a tile entity, marks itself dirty, notifies its six neighbours (flag 3) and queues a block change for watching players. PlayerInstance.flagChunkForUpdate merges the three markBlockForUpdate calls into one S23PacketBlockChange per tick. That packet carries the unchanged block and facing, so on the client Chunk.func_150807_a returns early and nothing re-renders; the cost is server-side work, neighbour updates and one packet per tick.
  - Evidence: `boolean trigger = true; if(hasPower() && canProcess() && this.progress == 0) { trigger = false; } if(trigger) { markDirty = true; MachineElectricFurnace.updateBlockState(this.progress > 0, this.worldObj, this.xCoord, this.yCoord, this.zCoord); }` (L215-224); `world.setBlock(x, y, z, ModBlocks.machine_electric_furnace_on);` / `_off` (MachineElectricFurnace.java:160, 162), `world.setBlockMetadataWithNotify(x, y, z, i, 2);` (L166), `entity.validate(); world.setTileEntity(x, y, z, entity);` (L169-170). javap: World.setBlock(IIILBlock;) passes meta 0 and flags 3; Chunk.func_150807_a returns false early only when block and meta are both unchanged, and otherwise calls Block.onBlockPreDestroy, Block.breakBlock, TileEntity.shouldRefresh and removeTileEntity, then Block.onBlockAdded and func_150806_e; PlayerManager$PlayerInstance.flagChunkForUpdate returns early for a position already queued; WorldClient.func_147492_c calls World.setBlock, which skips markBlockForUpdate when Chunk.func_150807_a returns false.
  - Fix: Call updateBlockState only when the wanted block differs from the current one (`worldObj.getBlock(xCoord, yCoord, zCoord) != (progress > 0 ? ModBlocks.machine_electric_furnace_on : ModBlocks.machine_electric_furnace_off)`), and pass the facing meta to setBlock instead of 0.
  - Plan: Phase 6
  - Status: open
- **B-420** · silent misconfig · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/machine/TileEntityMachinePumpBase.java:69-71`
  - Steam and electric pumps share the config name 'waterpump'; hbmMachines.json gets two blocks and only the last is read. TileEntityMachinePumpBase.getConfigName returns "waterpump" (L69-71) and neither TileEntityMachinePumpSteam nor TileEntityMachinePumpElectric overrides it, while both are registered configurables (TileMappings.java:344-345), so MachineDynConfig writes one "waterpump" object per dummy (L73-81) and hbmMachines.json holds two objects with the same name. On read, json.get(name) (L55) returns only the last of them (Gson's JsonObject keeps the last value of a repeated key), so an edit made only in the first block is silently ignored and the next start rewrites both blocks with the second block's values. The settings are shared static fields (L62-66), so both pumps use one set of values either way.
  - Evidence: `public String getConfigName() { return "waterpump"; }` (L69-71); `writer.name(dummy.getConfigName()).beginObject();` (MachineDynConfig.java:76); `JsonElement element = json.get(dummy.getConfigName());` (MachineDynConfig.java:55). Gson 2.2.4 (the pack's library) reads an object with JsonObject.add, which calls LinkedTreeMap.put, so the last duplicate wins. No other getConfigName value repeats.

- **B-066** · crash · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/machine/rbmk/TileEntityRBMKControlAuto.java:91-94,117-127`
  - TileEntityRBMKControlAuto: NBT without "function" leaves function null and crashes the server tick. readFromNBT (91-94) sets function=null when the NBT has no "function" key; writeToNBT (106-107) and serialize (117) then skip it while deserialize (127) always reads it. On the server, updateEntity:57 `switch(this.function)` NPEs once heat is inside the heatLower/heatUpper bounds, which is a 'Ticking block entity' server crash, and getSettings:177 (settings tool) and TileEntityRBMKConsole:621 (OC getColumnData, `controlAuto.function.toString()`) NPE as well; the client's extra readInt reads the zero padding the packet codec leaves after the written data (NetworkHandler.java:66; see the PrecompilingNetworkCodec padding entry), so it silently gets ordinal 0 (LINEAR) and GUIRBMKControlAuto:160 is unaffected. Latent: the mod never writes such NBT (the field starts as LINEAR at line 23, only readFromNBT:94 assigns null, writeToNBT writes the key whenever function is non-null, and no bundled structure .nbt contains this TE), so only hand-edited or foreign NBT, or a world last saved by the 2021-04-20 dev commit 6235e886d (before the field existed), triggers it.
  - Evidence: `if(nbt.hasKey("function")) this.function = RBMKFunction.values()[nbt.getInteger("function")]; else this.function = null;` (91-94); `if(function != null) buf.writeInt(function.ordinal()); ... this.function = RBMKFunction.values()[buf.readInt()];` (117, 127). Nothing in tileentity/machine/rbmk or TileEntityLoadedBase overrides getDescriptionPacket (vanilla returns null, javap), so the client never runs readFromNBT; the extra readInt reads the codec's zero padding instead of underflowing (it would throw, and BufPacket:58-63 would log it, only once that padding is removed). javap World.updateEntities: a TE tick exception becomes a ReportedException unless ForgeModContainer.removeErroringTileEntities is set (Property.getBoolean(false)). getSettings callers: ItemSettingsTool:87, BlockDummyable:613.
  - Fix: In readFromNBT use `function = nbt.hasKey("function") ? EnumUtil.grabEnumSafely(RBMKFunction.class, nbt.getInteger("function")) : RBMKFunction.LINEAR;` (this also stops a corrupt ordinal at :92 from throwing during load), and write the ordinal unconditionally in writeToNBT (106-107) and serialize (117).
  - Plan: Phase 1
  - Status: open

The ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException escapes NBTControlPacket.Handler (catches only IOException, NBTControlPacket:92); FML logs it and disconnects that client, and the server keeps running (robustness, not a crash).

Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) is MIN_VALUE, and MIN_VALUE % 3 == -2, MIN_VALUE % 5 == -3.

### UNINOS networks, packet threading (`networks`)

- **B-093** · crash · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/network/TileEntityPylonBase.java:80-82`
  - TileEntityPylonBase.addConnection dereferences a possibly null PowerNode. The node exists only after the TE's first server tick (TileEntityCableBaseNT L18-26), so addConnection NPEs on node.recentlyChanged when a pylon is wired in the same tick it was placed or, more commonly, after a server restart or singleplayer world reload when the wire start kept in the wiring item's NBT (ItemWiring L43-48) is a pylon whose chunk has not loaded since: ItemWiring L59-61 loads that chunk synchronously through getTileEntity, and the TE has not ticked yet (wires reach 100 blocks, TileEntityPylonLarge L38 and TileEntityConnectorSuper L16, beyond low view distances). The NPE is thrown during packet handling, so singleplayer crashes ('Ticking memory connection') and a dedicated server kicks the player ('Internal server error'). TileEntityPipelineBase.addConnection (L42-50) guards the same case by creating the node.
  - Evidence: `PowerNode node = Nodespace.getNode(worldObj, xCoord, yCoord, zCoord); node.recentlyChanged = true;` (L80-81, after `connected.add` at L78; markDirty() and markBlockForUpdate() follow at L84-89). javap: ChunkProviderServer.provideChunk calls loadChunk for a missing chunk (loadChunkOnProvideRequest defaults to true); NetworkSystem.networkTick throws ReportedException on a local channel and otherwise disconnects the player. A plain relog on a running dedicated server does not trigger it: chunk unload calls onChunkUnload, not invalidate, so the old node survives and getNode finds it.
  - Fix: When the node is null, build it with createNode() (it already includes the new `connected` entry), register it with Nodespace.createNode and assign this.node, without the extra node.addConnection; or guard only the node update (`if(node != null) { node.recentlyChanged = true; node.addConnection(...); }`), since the next updateEntity rebuilds the node from `connected`. Either way markDirty() and markBlockForUpdate() (L84-89) must still run: returning before L84 leaves the new `connected` entry unsaved and unsynced, so the client never draws the wire.
  - Note: If this fix adds node cleanup to validate, invalidate or onChunkUnload, put it in TileEntityCableBaseNT (or in a differently named method called from there), not in TileEntityPylonBase: ntmrba 1.3 in the owner's pack (found 2026-09-26) merges its own versions of those three methods into TileEntityPylonBase without @Overwrite and silently replaces any the fork adds there. Test with ntmrba's OPTIMIZE_WIRES on and off.
  - Plan: Phase 2
  - Status: open
- **B-094** · crash · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/uninos/UniNodespace.java:52-56`
  - UniNodespace.destroyNode(World, GenNode) NPEs when the world has no node map. The by-reference overload calls worlds.get(world).popNode(node) with no null check; it has 13 call sites in 10 fusion and HTR-Neo classes, all in invalidate(). The entry can only be missing after /ntmreapnetworks (worlds.clear()): a TE holds a non-null node only after UniNodespace.createNode created the world's UniNodeWorld (L36-43) or getNode found the node in one, and nothing else removes entries. The trigger is breaking a fusion or HTR-Neo machine after the command and before any TE in that world has re-created an expired node (same packet batch as the command, or an entity or explosion early in the next tick), so this is an admin-command race rather than normal play; the NPE is thrown from invalidate() during block removal. The (x,y,z,provider) overload is null-safe.

The only remover of world entries is CommandReapNetworks L36; it marks net-linked nodes expired (L30), and Klystron handleKNode (L159-168), HTRNeo (L112-121) and cables recreate expired nodes, which re-creates the entry. javap World.updateEntities: entities update before tile entities, and invalidate() is called only in the removeErroringTileEntities branch (chunk unload calls onChunkUnload).
  - Fix: Null-check the UniNodeWorld before popNode and set node.expired = true when it is missing. Low priority on its own, but land it before the B-101 by-reference option and B-107, which rely on this overload.

  - waitUntilThreadFinished drops queued packets after 50 ms and latches to sync. Each Future gets a 50 ms wait (L150); on timeout the whole queue is cleared (L157-160), and after clearCnt > 5 (6th non-empty clear) hasTriggered latches and addTask (L133-134) runs every send inline until /ntmpackets resetState (CommandPacketInfo L34-37).   - Threaded send re-serializes every packet on the worker thread. Reusing a packet would throw IllegalReferenceCountException, but no caller does (every threaded caller passes a fresh packet; the only variable is the single-use local in TileEntityLoadedBase.networkPackNT L91-106).

- **B-353** · crash · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/commands/CommandPacketInfo.java:43-51`
  - /ntmpackets forceLock over RCON freezes the server tick. MinecraftServer.handleRConCommand runs the command on the RCON client thread, so forceLock (L44) makes that thread the owner of PacketThreading.lock, and the server thread blocks with no timeout at its next non-worker send (NetworkHandler.java:137/154/171/188/205) or inline packet task (PacketThreading.java:95/121, run inline when threading is off or hasTriggered has latched, L132-139). Only forceUnlock over the same RCON connection releases it: ReentrantLock.unlock from any other thread throws IllegalMonitorStateException, players and the console are frozen with the server thread, and if that RCON connection closes the lock is held forever. Issued in-game, from the console or from a command block the command runs on the server thread, the lock re-enters and only the worker starves (waitUntilThreadFinished times out after 50 ms at PacketThreading.java:150, clears the queue and after more than 5 clears latches synchronous sends, L193-206). RCON exists only on a dedicated server with enable-rcon=true (off by default).

NetworkHandler takes the lock whenever `!Thread.currentThread().getName().contains(PacketThreading.threadPrefix)` (L135, 152, 169, 186, 203). Player commands reach the server thread because C01PacketChatMessage has no hasPriority override (Packet.hasPriority returns false), and DedicatedServer.updateTimeLightAndEntities runs console commands through executePendingCommands.
  - Fix: Refuse forceLock/forceUnlock when the sender is RConConsoleSource or the calling thread is not the server thread (CommandPacketInfo.java:43-51).
  - Note: previously listed under "Reviewed and rejected" with the reason "ReentrantLock re-enters on the owning server thread; forceLock only starves the worker", which holds for every sender except RCON.
  - Plan: Phase 5
  - Status: open

Guns (ItemGunBaseNT) and universal grenades (ItemGrenadeUniversal) are unaffected because each fires onEquip itself from a per-stack 'eqipped' NBT edge detector in onUpdate; the only gap there is a stack whose flag is stale-true (it left the held slot without being ticked unheld, e.g. on the cursor) being swapped into the held slot over the same Item.   - ItemBookLore and ItemBedrockOreNew index their overlay arrays by render pass without bounds checks; MorePlayerModels' extra pass throws. ItemBookLore.getRenderPasses returns 3 (L82) while overlays holds two icons (L72), and getIconFromDamageForRenderPass returns overlays[pass - 1] (L88); ItemBedrockOreNew returns 1 + traits.length passes (L90) and indexes traits[pass - 1] (L96). ### Weapons, projectiles, missiles (`weapons`)

- **B-119** · gameplay · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/entity/projectile/EntityArtilleryRocket.java:34-35`
  - EntityArtilleryRocket keeps a raw Entity target reference. targetEntity (L35, TODO at L34) is a plain Entity field that is never persisted: writeEntityToNBT/readEntityFromNBT (L191-213) store only lastTargetPos (targetX/Y/Z) and type, so after a world restart the rocket reloads with targetEntity == null and steers to the last predicted lastTargetPos without tracking. The rocket's own chunk stays force-loaded (loadNeighboringChunks every server tick, L118, L162-176; only a null ticket from requestTicket at L51 breaks this), so only the target can unload mid-flight: World.updateEntities then drops it from loadedEntityList without setting isDead, L105 isEntityAlive() stays true, and RocketTargetingPredictive (L114) keeps predicting from the frozen position and motion; the new object created when the target's chunk reloads is never re-acquired. Minor: a flight lasts a few seconds.
  - Evidence: `L34 '//TODO: find satisfying solution for when an entity is unloaded and reloaded...' L35 'public Entity targetEntity = null;'`; L199-203 write only targetX/Y/Z and type. javap (Forge jar): World.unloadEntities only does unloadedEntityList.addAll; updateEntities does loadedEntityList.removeAll, Chunk.removeEntity and onEntityRemoved, none of which sets isDead; Chunk.removeEntityAtIndex never clears Entity.addedToChunk; WorldServer.getEntityByID reads entityIdMap, which WorldServer.onEntityRemoved clears; the only UUID lookup is World.func_152378_a(UUID), which returns EntityPlayer; Entity NBT carries UUIDMost/UUIDLeast.
  - Fix: Write targetEntity.getUniqueID() in writeEntityToNBT. In the server branch of onUpdate treat the target as missing or stale when `targetEntity == null || worldObj.getEntityByID(targetEntity.getEntityId()) != targetEntity` (or `!worldObj.loadedEntityList.contains(targetEntity)`), clear targetEntity while it is unresolved, and while a UUID is stored re-resolve every N ticks: worldObj.func_152378_a(uuid) for players, otherwise a scan of worldObj.loadedEntityList for a matching getUniqueID(). Resolve lazily in onUpdate, never in readEntityFromNBT (the other entities are not loaded yet), and do not test targetEntity.addedToChunk, which a chunk unload does not clear.
  - Plan: Phase 6
  - Status: open

- **B-123** · gameplay · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/items/weapon/sedna/mods/WeaponModCaliber.java:16-51`
  - WeaponModCaliber returns shared static DUMMY_* magazines mutated per eval. eval() mutates the class-static DUMMY_SINGLE/DUMMY_FULL/DUMMY_BELT (acceptedBullets, capacity, index) and returns them, so every caliber mod of every gun hands out the same three objects and magazine identity cannot be used as a key. The realistic hazard is cross-thread on an integrated server or LAN host: the client thread (HUD, tooltip, render) evaluates one config while the server thread evaluates another and re-points index, and MagazineSingleTypeBase keys the count and type NBT on this.index (L231-241), so a stale index reads or writes the other config's count. No current same-thread caller holds the returned magazine across another O_MAGAZINE eval (sampled: Lego.doStandardFire, ItemGunBaseNT.addInformation, the orchestra lambdas all use it immediately).

  - Fix: Allocate a fresh magazine per eval (e.g. `new MagazineFullReload(original.index, count)` with acceptedBullets = cfg, the same for MagazineSingleReload), or cache one instance per (mod, base magazine) in a ConcurrentHashMap or IdentityHashMap keyed on the base magazine instance. A per-mod instance is not enough for the single and full magazines, because one mod instance serves configs whose magazines have index 0 and 1; a per-mod belt instance is enough (belts have no index and each mod's cfg list is constant).

- **B-176** · dead code · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/entity/EntityMappings.java:82-86`
  - Duplicate entity name entity_cloud_rainbow for two classes. No save impact can be observed: maxAge lives only in DataWatcher 16 and is not persisted, so a reloaded or summoned cloud of either class dies on its first tick, and live clouds render correctly because the client spawns by numeric id and renderers are bound per class (ClientProxy.java:745-746). Registry hygiene, not save data.
  - Evidence: `L82 addEntity(EntityCloudFleijaRainbow.class, "entity_cloud_rainbow", 1000); L86 addEntity(EntityCloudSolinium.class, "entity_cloud_rainbow", 1000);`. javap: FML EntityRegistry.doModEntityRegistration (57-117) writes EntityList.classToStringMapping/stringToClassMapping for each class not yet mapped, so the string ends up pointing at the second class; entityNames is a plain HashMap, so the duplicate throws nothing. The two classes differ only in the client-only isInRangeToRenderDist override (EntityCloudFleijaRainbow.java:85-90); readEntityFromNBT (L65-68 in both) restores only age and scale, so getMaxAge()==0 and onUpdate (L55-58) calls setDead(). No lang key uses either name.

- **B-177** · save data · needs a decision · `src/main/java/com/hbm/entity/logic/EntityNukeExplosionMK5.java:144-151`
  - MK5 nuke explosion loses all state on save/reload. Only ticksExisted is persisted; strength/speed/length/fallout are not, so a reloaded in-progress MK5 explosion has strength 0 and setDead()s on its first tick (L56-59): the crater stops half-done and no fallout is spawned. MK3 (L50-116), Balefire (L32-57) and Tom (L24-48) persist their state.
  - Evidence: `readEntityFromNBT: this.ticksExisted = nbt.getInteger("ticksExisted"); onUpdate: if(strength == 0) { clearChunkLoader(); setDead(); return; }`. The ray progress is ExplosionNukeRayBatched.perChunk (L20): one FloatTriplet per ray per non-air chunk it crosses (L130-139) over gspNumMax = 2.5*pi*strength^2 rays (L47), about 452k rays for r=120; a simulated flat-stone r=120 blast needs about 2.3 MB compressed. javap: RegionFile.write (23-43) returns without writing when the compressed chunk needs >= 256 sectors of 4 KiB (1 MiB), so entity NBT that large silently drops the whole chunk save. The explosion object is transient, so a reloaded entity re-enters the explosion == null branch (L74-83) and calls SatelliteDetector.reportEvent (L82) again; salted (L36) is not persisted either.
  - Fix: Persist strength, speed, length, fallout and falloutAdd (plus salted once the missing `fallout.setSalted` call is restored) in writeEntityToNBT/readEntityFromNBT, and let onUpdate build a fresh ExplosionNukeRayBatched on load. Nothing is destroyed during collection (destructionTick returns until isAusf3Complete, L269), so a mid-collection save loses nothing; after a mid-destruction save the rays re-collect over the partly cleared crater, so hard terrain may end up with a slightly larger crater, still capped at length. Never serialise perChunk into entity NBT (the chunk coordinates in orderedChunks are small and could be kept if wanted). Guard reportEvent with a persisted flag, and pair this with B-186 (write milliTime and honour limitExplosionLifespan).
  - Plan: decision D20
  - Status: open

- **B-181** · gameplay · needs a decision · `src/main/java/com/hbm/entity/logic/EntityNukeExplosionMK5.java:68-80`
  - MK5 radiate() skips its first and strongest pulse. radiate() requires explosion != null, but the explosion object is only created later in the first tick (L74-80); because World increments ticksExisted before calling onUpdate, the first onUpdate already sees ticksExisted=1, so pulses run at ticksExisted 2-9 (8 pulses) instead of 1-9. The skipped pulse, 2.5e6/6 = 416,667, is the largest (the tick-2 pulse is 227,273), so restoring it raises the total prompt radiation dose by about 48%: a balance change, not a harmless one-liner.
  - Evidence: `L68-69: if(!isRemote && fallout && explosion != null && ticksExisted < 10 && strength >= 75) radiate(2_500_000F / (this.ticksExisted * 5 + 1), this.length * 2); explosion created later at L74-80`. javap: World.updateEntityWithOptionalForce increments ticksExisted (when addedToChunk) before calling onUpdate (167-203), and MK5 overrides onUpdate without calling super. Sum of 1/(5t+1): 0.3457 for t=2..9, 0.5123 for t=1..9 (x1.48); the per-target res and len^2 divisors scale every pulse the same way. A tick-0 pulse can never happen, whatever the guard.
  - Fix: Move the radiate() call below the explosion == null block, or drop the explosion != null guard (mechanically correct; about +48% prompt dose for MK5 nukes with strength >= 75), or leave as is.
  - Plan: decision D37
  - Status: open

- **B-185** · leak / perf · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/entity/logic/EntityExplosionChunkloading.java:22-44`
  - EntityExplosionChunkloading forces chunk (0,0) instead of the entity's chunk. init() runs from entityInit() inside the Entity constructor, before the entity is added to a chunk, so chunkCoordX/Z are still 0 and every MK3/MK5/Balefire/Tom/FalloutRain entity force-loads chunk (0,0) of its dimension until its ticket is released (FalloutRain reaches it via super.entityInit, L241-242). EntityTomBlast never calls clearChunkLoader (it dies at L82), and neither does the MK3 statFacFleija anti-tamper path (setDead at L237), so their tickets keep chunk (0,0) forced until the world unloads and count against the mod's per-world ticket quota. Balefire and FalloutRain never call loadChunk, so their own chunk is forced only through the ticketsLoaded callback after a reload (MainRegistry.java:374-375). On client worlds requestTicket (L23) also succeeds, and those tickets are never released because init and clearChunkLoader require !isRemote (harmless, bounded by the quota). loadChunk itself ignores later coordinates once loadedChunk is set (latent: every caller passes the stationary entity's own chunk), and a null ticket from the quota is only logged once per mod by Forge.
  - Evidence: `entityInit: init(ForgeChunkManager.requestTicket(MainRegistry.instance, worldObj, Type.ENTITY)); init: ... ForgeChunkManager.forceChunk(loaderTicket, new ChunkCoordIntPair(chunkCoordX, chunkCoordZ)); loadChunk: if(this.loadedChunk == null) { this.loadedChunk = new ChunkCoordIntPair(x, z); ForgeChunkManager.forceChunk(loaderTicket, loadedChunk); }`. javap: Entity.<init> sets worldObj, calls setPosition(0,0,0), then entityInit (110-174), and only Chunk.addEntity writes chunkCoordX/Z; ForgeChunkManager.forceChunk returns at once on a null ticket (0-8); requestTicket logs 'attempted to allocate a chunkloading ticket beyond it's currently allocated maximum' once per mod (warnedMods) and returns null (95-179); loadWorld registers ticket maps for client worlds before its WorldServer check. loadChunk callers: MK5 L62 and statFac L168, MK3 L126 and statFacFleija L264, TomBlast L58. The quota is forgeChunkLoading.cfg maximumTicketCount (default 200, ForgeChunkManager.java:799), shared with NTM's NORMAL tickets (ChunkLoaderManager.java:45); saveWorld skips entity tickets whose entity is dead, so leaked tickets vanish on restart. The moving chunkloaders with the same init (EntityMissileBaseNT.java:322, EntityPlaneBase.java:84, EntityArtilleryShell.java:189) unforce every ticket chunk in loadNeighboringChunks on their next update (EntityMissileBaseNT.java:327-337, EntityPlaneBase.java:198-206), so for them (0,0) is forced only briefly.
  - Fix: In entityInit only request and bind the ticket, and only when !worldObj.isRemote; force the entity's real chunk in loadChunk or on the first server tick, and call loadChunk from EntityBalefire and EntityFalloutRain. Call clearChunkLoader on every death path (EntityTomBlast L82, MK3 statFacFleija L237). In loadChunk, unforce the previous chunk and force the new one when the coordinates differ, and log when loaderTicket is null.
  - Note: needs in-game verification: after a reload, entityInit binds a fresh ticket before ForgeChunkManager.loadWorld calls ticketsLoaded, so init(ticket) re-forces the real chunk with that fresh loaderTicket (released normally), while the restored ticket stays registered and is never released: one quota slot per reloaded explosion until restart (source reading of ForgeChunkManager.loadWorld and init L27-36). Test by reloading during an MK3 or Balefire explosion, then checking forced chunks and whether the ticket count returns to its previous value after the explosion ends.
  - Plan: Phase 5
  - Status: open

- **B-188** · leak / perf · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/explosion/ExplosionNukeRayBatched.java:260-264`
  - ExplosionNukeRayBatched.cacheChunksTick ignores its time budget. cacheChunksTick(time) discards the ms budget and always runs collectTip(speed*10), so BombConfig.mk5 bounds only the destruction phase. Each collection tick casts 10*floor(100000/strength) rays of up to this.length (= strength/2) steps, about 500k ray steps for any radius (r=25 finishes in one tick, r=500 takes about 7,854 ticks), plus synchronous loading or generation of every unloaded chunk the rays touch, which does grow with radius. MK5 L85-87 also runs destructionTick in the tick where collection completes, so that tick can spend up to about 2x the mk5 budget.

EntityNukeExplosionMK5.java:165 `mk5.speed = (int)Math.ceil(100000 / mk5.strength);` (integer division first). collectTip returns at the count limit (L145-147); a `break` out of the while (L85) would fall through to L150-153, which fill orderedChunks and set isAusf3Complete=true with most rays never cast. javap: ChunkProviderServer.provideChunk calls loadChunk synchronously when loadChunkOnProvideRequest is set (default true), so world.getBlock at L111 loads or generates chunks inside the tick.
  - Fix: Pass the budget into collectTip(count, timeMs), record start = System.currentTimeMillis(), and `return` (not break) from inside the while once the time passes start + timeMs, keeping count as a cap. Optionally skip destructionTick in the tick where collection finished.

- **B-374** · leak / perf · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/entity/missile/EntityMissileBaseNT.java:99-104,310-325`
  - Moving IChunkLoader entities force chunk (0,0) from entityInit and never adopt restored tickets. EntityMissileBaseNT and its subclasses (including EntityMissileCustom and EntityRideableRocket), EntityMissileAntiBallistic, EntityPlaneBase, EntityArtilleryShell, EntityArtilleryRocket and EntityBulletBaseMK4CL call init(requestTicket(...ENTITY)) from entityInit(), which Entity(World) runs before the entity has a position or a chunk, so init() forces (chunkCoordX, chunkCoordZ) = (0,0) of the dimension. The force is brief: it lasts until the entity's first loadNeighboringChunks call (every server tick from onUpdate), which unforces the ticket's whole chunk list before forcing the current chunk. Separately, persisted ENTITY tickets restored on world load are never adopted: entityInit has already bound a fresh loaderTicket by the time ForgeChunkManager.loadWorld calls ticketsLoaded, init keeps that one and forces through it, and clearChunkLoader releases only loaderTicket. The restored ticket stays in Forge's ticket map, forcing nothing but counting against the mod's per-world ticket quota, until the world unloads (saveWorld stops re-saving it once the entity is dead). EntityDeliveryDrone has only the second problem: it requests its ticket from readEntityFromNBT, so after a reload it too already holds a fresh loaderTicket when the restored one arrives. The explosion entities (EntityExplosionChunkloading subclasses) are covered by B-185.
  - Evidence: EntityMissileBaseNT.java:102 `init(ForgeChunkManager.requestTicket(MainRegistry.instance, worldObj, Type.ENTITY));`; init (L310-325) binds the passed ticket only `if(loaderTicket == null)` and then calls `ForgeChunkManager.forceChunk(loaderTicket, new ChunkCoordIntPair(chunkCoordX, chunkCoordZ));` (L322); loadNeighboringChunks (L327-338, called at L164 on every server tick) unforces each chunk of getChunkList() before forcing the new one; clearChunkLoader (L346-351) releases only loaderTicket. EntityMissileCustom (L105-106) and EntityRideableRocket (L856-857) reach it through super.entityInit(). The same entityInit/init/loadNeighboringChunks set is at EntityMissileAntiBallistic:46/184-199/203-217, EntityPlaneBase:72/77-86/198-207, EntityArtilleryShell:61/182-191/195-210, EntityArtilleryRocket:51/149-158/162-177 and EntityBulletBaseMK4CL:34/38-47/69-83. EntityDeliveryDrone: readEntityFromNBT L132 -> setChunkLoading L68-71; init L223-232 keeps an existing loaderTicket. javap: Entity(World) calls setPosition(0,0,0) at bc 117 and entityInit at bc 174 and never writes chunkCoordX; only Chunk.addEntity sets chunkCoordX/Z. Forge ForgeChunkManager.java: loadWorld builds restored tickets without a chunk list (L454), loadEntity binds each to its entity (L885-894), and the tickets are put into the world's ticket map (L522) before ticketsLoaded runs (L523); requestTicket returns null once that map holds getMaxTicketLengthFor(modId) tickets (L667-677; maximumTicketCount, default 200, L799); saveWorld writes an ENTITY ticket only while tick.entity.writeToNBTOptional succeeds (L860), which javap shows returns false once isDead is set.
  - Fix: Skip the forceChunk in each init() while !addedToChunk (the first server-side onUpdate forces the real chunk through loadNeighboringChunks; after a world load the loading callback runs with addedToChunk true), or request the ticket lazily on the first server-side onUpdate instead of in entityInit. When init(ticket) is called from the loading callback while loaderTicket is already set, release the passed ticket (ForgeChunkManager.releaseTicket) or adopt it and release the construction-time one; EntityDeliveryDrone.init needs the same adopt-or-release. Do together with B-004 (the loading callback) and B-185 (the same pattern in EntityExplosionChunkloading).

### Hazards, radiation, pollution, atmosphere, saved data (`hazards`)

- **B-193** · crash · needs a decision · `src/main/java/com/hbm/handler/atmosphere/AtmosphereBlob.java:171-179`
  - AtmosphereBlob runs its flood fill and applies the result on a pool thread. With GeneralConfig.enableThreadedAtmospheres (default true, GeneralConfig.java:84/132) addBlock hands run() to a ThreadPoolExecutor, and the pool thread reads blocks while the server thread mutates chunks; a chunk unloaded between the L79 chunkExists check and the L82 getBlock is reloaded through provideChunk from the pool thread. A failed flood also removes blocks and spawns EntityDepress from the pool thread, and a successful one writes the plants map that checkGrowth iterates on the server thread, so a ConcurrentModificationException can hit the server tick. The static fullBounds HashMap (L50) is shared unsynchronised by the pool and main-thread callers.
  - Evidence: `if(GeneralConfig.enableThreadedAtmospheres) { try { pool.execute(this); } ...} else { this.run(); }` (L171-179). Reads off-thread: isBlockSealed L79 chunkExists, L82 getBlock, L88 IBlockSealable.isSealed; addSingleBlock L187; addPlant L398; clearBlob via L355. - **B-214** · gameplay · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/handler/ThreeInts.java:46-48`
  - ThreeInts.compareTo breaks HashMap/HashSet lookups in treeified bins. compareTo returns 1 for every unequal pair (never negative). Java 8 HashMap/HashSet order keys of a class that implements Comparable<itself> by compareTo once a bin is treeified (9+ entries in one bucket, table 64+), and ThreeInts's linear 31-based hashCode (L17-25) makes (x, y+1, z-31) and (x+1, y-31, z) collide with (x, y, z), so large volumes build big equal-hash groups and get contains()/get() false negatives and duplicate inserts. Latent for small sets, live for large ones: AtmosphereBlob's flood fill (HashSet addableBlocks, AdjacencyGraph HashMap, plants LinkedHashMap; blob radius up to 256) relies on contains() to avoid rescanning, and AdjacencyGraph.add dereferences get() of neighbours without a null check, so a miss can NPE on the atmosphere thread. Fields x/y/z are public and mutable, but only the constructor writes them.
  - Evidence: `public class ThreeInts implements Comparable<ThreeInts>` (L5); `public int compareTo(ThreeInts o) { return equals(o) ? 0 : 1; }` (L46-48); hashed users AtmosphereBlob.java:60 (plants), :206 and :291 (HashSets), :298-307 (flood fill relies on contains), AdjacencyGraph.java:48-56 (`adjacencyMatrix.get(iterator.next()).add(object)` at L54), OrbitalStation.java:65 and :297, IToolAreaAbility.java:91, ChunkLoaderManager.java:91; TileEntityAirPump.java:298 getMaxBlobRadius() returns 256. Runtime test on OpenJDK 1.8.0_462 with a verbatim copy of ThreeInts: 0 misses up to 64x32x64, but 8,700 contains() misses in a 12x12x300 box, 10,760 in 8x16x300, 17,780 in 128x40x128 and 555,958 of 1,000,000 in 100^3; 32 of 40 equal-hash keys missed, with 38 duplicate adds; a lexicographic compareTo gave 0 misses in every case.
  - Fix: Implement a lexicographic compare (x, then y, then z) or drop Comparable; optionally make the fields final (compiles: the only other `.x/.y/.z` writes in ThreeInts-using files are Growth's own fields, ChunkAtmosphereHandler.java:491-493) and use a mixing hashCode so large volumes stop treeifying.
  - Plan: Phase 6
  - Status: open

- **B-384** · gameplay · needs a decision · `src/main/java/com/hbm/handler/radiation/ChunkRadiationHandlerSimple.java:94-102`
  - Simple radiation spread overwrites contributions to chunks without an entry. In updateSystem a neighbour coordinate that had no entry in the previous cycle is written with `radiation.put(newCoord, chunk.getValue() * percent)` instead of being added to, so when two or more radiating chunks border the same fresh coordinate in one cycle only the last one's share survives and the rest is lost (that branch also skips the 0.99/-0.05 decay the other branch applies). Radiation therefore spreads outward more slowly than the weights (0.6 self, 0.075 edge, 0.025 corner) intend. The other branch has the clamp arguments swapped: `clamp_float(0F, newRad * 0.99F - 0.05F, maxRad)` returns max(0, v) and never applies maxRad, which is harmless in practice because the weights sum to 1.0 and setRadiation clamps its input (L54).
  - Evidence: L94-102 `if(buff.containsKey(newCoord)) { ... newRad = MathHelper.clamp_float(0F, newRad * 0.99F - 0.05F, maxRad); radiation.put(newCoord, newRad); } else { radiation.put(newCoord, chunk.getValue() * percent); }`; javap MathHelper.clamp_float(float,float,float): returns arg1 if arg0 < arg1, arg2 if arg0 > arg2, else arg0.
  - Fix: Accumulate in the else branch (`Float v = radiation.get(newCoord); radiation.put(newCoord, (v == null ? 0F : v) + chunk.getValue() * percent);`) and write the clamp as `MathHelper.clamp_float(newRad * 0.99F - 0.05F, 0F, maxRad)`. The first change makes radiation spread into new chunks faster than today.

- **B-389** · leak / perf · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/saveddata/SatelliteSavedData.java:84-98`
  - Satellite lookups from orbit hot-load the orbited body's dimension, every tick through PermaSync. SatelliteSavedData.getData(World, x, z) resolves the station's orbited body and calls DimensionManager.initDimension when that world is not loaded (L84-98); XSatelliteRegistry.orbit does the same (XSatelliteRegistry.java:76, 83-90). PermaSyncHandler.writePacket calls getData for the player's position (PermaSyncHandler.java:118-123), and ModEventHandler.onPlayerTick sends every player a PermaSyncPacket every server tick (ModEventHandler.java:1481; PermaSyncPacket.toBytes runs writePacket, PermaSyncPacket.java:27-28). Planet dimensions are registered with keepLoaded = false (PlanetGen.java:70), so a hot-loaded world with no loaded chunk queues its own unload on its next tick and is saved and unloaded at the end of that tick, and the next PermaSync creates it again: while a player is in orbit around a body nobody is on, the server keeps constructing, saving and unloading a WorldServerMulti and firing WorldEvent.Load/Unload. Only a player or a ForgeChunkManager ticket there keeps it loaded: chunks loaded without one are queued for unload by PlayerManager.updatePlayerInstances (unloadAllChunks when the world has no players and the provider's canRespawnHere is false, which WorldProviderCelestial.java:696-703 returns outside sleeping), so the cycle continues.

Forge DimensionManager.initDimension (L226-254) builds the WorldServerMulti and posts WorldEvent.Load; unloadWorlds (L315-340) saves it, posts WorldEvent.Unload and drops it. javap forgeBin: ChunkProviderServer.unloadQueuedChunks calls DimensionManager.unloadWorld when loadedChunks.size() == 0, no persistent chunks and !shouldLoadSpawn (offsets 167-218); WorldServer.tick calls unloadQueuedChunks (offset 165); MinecraftServer.updateTimeLightAndEntities calls DimensionManager.unloadWorlds (offset 365); PlayerManager.updatePlayerInstances calls ChunkProviderServer.unloadAllChunks when players.isEmpty() and !canRespawnHere() (offsets 123-158).

Keep initDimension only on write paths (XSatelliteRegistry.orbit, SatelliteHorizons.java:74), which must mark the target world's data dirty.

  - AtmosphereBlob.fullBounds caches whatever bounds a pane block had at the first query, so panes seal or leak per run. isBlockSealed decides sealing for ordinary solid blocks from getCollisionBoundingBoxFromPool(null, x, y, z) and caches the answer per Block in a static map (L50, L96-122). The first sealing query of a session therefore caches panes as full, sealing blocks if the shared fields are full at that moment (for example right after a dedicated-server start) and as never sealing otherwise; in singleplayer the client's collisions, ray traces and item rendering mutate the same Block instances, so the outcome also depends on client activity.

BlockNTMGlassPane.java:13 extends BlockPane.

Audit other blocks that override setBlockBoundsBasedOnState but not getCollisionBoundingBoxFromPool the same way.

- **B-219** · gameplay · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/dim/ChunkProviderCelestial.java:415`
  - ChunkProviderCelestial.populate clears isHellWorld until the next world tick. populate sets worldObj.provider.isHellWorld = false so that world generators do not treat the planet as the Nether, and the flag stays false until WorldProviderCelestial/WorldProviderOrbit.updateWeather recomputes it at the start of that world's next tick (World.tick -> updateWeather -> provider.updateWeather). Player actions are processed in NetworkSystem.networkTick after all world ticks, so after any chunk population on an airless body a water bucket can be emptied there (ItemBucket.tryPlaceContainedLiquid reads isHellWorld) and broken ice turns into water (BlockIce.harvestBlock reads it too) until the next tick.
  - Evidence: `worldObj.provider.isHellWorld = false; // Prevent other mod world generators thinking this is hell` (L415; L414 is BlockFalling.fallInstantly = true). javap: ChunkProviderServer.populate calls IChunkProvider.populate (offset 35) and only then GameRegistry.generateWorld (offset 51), so every IWorldGenerator (other mods' and NTM's own HbmWorldGen, NTMWorldGenerator, WorldGeneratorCelestial) runs after populate returns; MinecraftServer.updateTimeLightAndEntities runs NetworkSystem.networkTick (offset 382) after all WorldServer.tick calls. The same clear-and-let-updateWeather-restore idiom is used on purpose at ModEventHandler.java:661-662 and DispenserBehaviorHandler.java:93-94.
  - Fix: Do not restore the flag at the end of populate: the generators the line protects run after populate returns. Option (a): register a trivial IWorldGenerator with weight Integer.MAX_VALUE (FML sorts generators ascending with Ints.compare, so it runs last) that recomputes isHellWorld for WorldProviderCelestial/WorldProviderOrbit with the same formula as their updateWeather (WorldProviderCelestial.java:94-99, WorldProviderOrbit.java:81-82; factor it into a helper); it covers every consumer of the flag, but a cascading population runs the restorer for the neighbour chunk while the outer chunk's later generators are still pending. Option (b), narrower but robust against cascades: in ModEventHandler.onBucketUse (non-CoFH branch, L660-663) set event.world.provider.isHellWorld = !hasLiquidPressure instead of only clearing it, and do the same in DispenserBehaviorHandler's water-bucket override (L93-95); this works because FillBucketEvent fires in ItemBucket.onItemRightClick before tryPlaceContainedLiquid, and onBucketUse is already limited to celestial/orbit providers (L649). Option (b) leaves ice breaking in the window.

- **B-220** · gameplay · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/dim/WorldProviderCelestial.java:693-703`
  - WorldProviderCelestial.canRespawnHere static sleep flag leaks when the bed is never activated. canRespawnHere returns true once after the global static attemptingSleep was set by ModEventHandler.onTrySleep (L1833-1840, any server RIGHT_CLICK_BLOCK on a BlockBed in a celestial/orbit dim) and clears it; WorldProviderOrbit.canRespawnHere (L224-231) consumes the same flag. Server logic is single-threaded and set and consume normally happen inside one ItemInWorldManager.activateBlockOrUseItem call, so concurrent sleeps do not race; the flag leaks when the click never reaches BlockBed.onBlockActivated's canRespawnHere call (a lower-priority handler cancels the event, useBlock is DENY, Item.onItemUseFirst returns true, the player sneaks with a held item that does not bypass, or the bed's head half is missing). The next canRespawnHere() in any celestial/orbit world then consumes it: PlayerManager.updatePlayerInstances for an empty world, ChunkProviderServer.unloadChunksIfNotNearSpawn, WorldServer.createSpawnPosition, or ServerConfigurationManager.respawnPlayer, which then skips getRespawnDimension (L676-689) and respawns the player on the planet without the breathable-bed check.
  - Evidence: `public static boolean attemptingSleep = false; ... if(attemptingSleep) { attemptingSleep = false; return true; } return false;` (L693-703). javap: ItemInWorldManager.activateBlockOrUseItem returns on a cancelled event (offsets 20-23) and when onItemUseFirst returns true (80-102), and skips Block.onBlockActivated for a sneaking player whose held item does not bypass (doesSneakBypassUse) or for useBlock DENY (129-220); BlockBed.onBlockActivated returns at offset 71 (head half missing) before canRespawnHere at 86; ServerConfigurationManager.respawnPlayer calls canRespawnHere at offset 25 and getRespawnDimension (offset 37) only when it returns false.
  - Fix: Make the flag an instance field of the clicked world's provider and set it in a LOWEST-priority handler only when activation can proceed: !event.isCanceled(), event.useBlock != DENY, and (!player.isSneaking() || player.getHeldItem() == null || heldItem.getItem().doesSneakBypassUse(world, x, y, z, player)), mirroring ItemInWorldManager. Clear it at ServerTickEvent END, because onItemUseFirst cannot be predicted (interact packets are processed in networkTick after every WorldTickEvent END, so clearing at WorldTickEvent END would leave it set into the next tick). Alternative: cancel the bed interaction in these dims and replicate BlockBed's sleep path (sleepInBedAt plus the occupied-flag update) so canRespawnHere can always return false. Do not return true unconditionally: respawnPlayer consults getRespawnDimension only when canRespawnHere is false, and empty celestial worlds would keep chunks loaded (PlayerManager.updatePlayerInstances and ChunkProviderServer.unloadChunksIfNotNearSpawn branch on it).
  - Plan: Phase 6
  - Status: open

The writes without markDirty (updateSwarms L458-466, trait.update at ModEventHandler.java:1545-1548) mutate trait objects, not the map, so a map copy would not affect them.

  - An emptied trait override is cleared, reverting the body to its default traits. Bodies whose defaults hold another trait besides CBT_Atmosphere (Kerbin, Eve, Laythe, Tekto) keep a non-empty map, and bodies without a default atmosphere revert to the same airless state, so Duna is the visible case.

  - Fix: Store an empty map instead of calling clearTraits when traits.length == 0, keeping clearTraits as the explicit revert. Pair with B-231, whose deep-copy fix makes the revert immediate in every case.

  - Status: open
