- **B-398** · gameplay · needs a decision · `src/main/java/com/hbm/world/gen/NTMWorldGenerator.java:256-320`
  - NTMWorldGenerator shares one GenStructure, with its structure map and saved data, across all dimensions. A single nbtGen (L256), replaced on every WorldEvent.Load (L262-267), serves the overworld, the Nether, the End and every planet until the next load. NBTStructure.GenStructure (NBTStructure.java:1247-1255) inherits MapGenStructure's instance state unchanged: structureMap is keyed by chunk coordinates only, and the MapGenStructureData is loaded from the perWorldStorage of the first world that asks and then reused for every world. A structure start made in one dimension therefore (a) blocks a start at the same chunk key in another dimension, because recursiveGenerate checks structureMap.containsKey before canSpawnStructureAtCoords, (b) is built into any other dimension's chunk that its bounding box intersects, because generateStructuresInChunk tests only the box, and (c) is saved into whichever world's data/NBTStructures.dat was loaded first, and restored into the shared map whenever a fresh nbtGen loads that file first (after a restart or any later WorldEvent.Load). The per-dimension spawn rules in getSpawnAtCoords (NBTStructure.java:1284-1330) only decide where new starts are made. B-227 covers the shared hasPopulationEvent flag, not this state.
  - Evidence: `private NBTStructure.GenStructure nbtGen = new NBTStructure.GenStructure();` (L256); `nbtGen = (NBTStructure.GenStructure) TerrainGen.getModdedMapGen(new NBTStructure.GenStructure(), EventType.CUSTOM);` (L264); both generation paths call nbtGen.generateStructures (L294, L311), and getStructureAt (L320, used by /ntmlocate) reads the same instance. javap forgeBin MapGenStructure: fields `private MapGenStructureData field_143029_e` and `protected Map structureMap`; func_143027_a loads the data only when the field is null (offsets 1-25, world.perWorldStorage.loadData); func_151538_a returns early when structureMap.containsKey(chunkXZ2Int) (offsets 6-22) and otherwise puts and saves the new start (offsets 51-75); generateStructuresInChunk iterates structureMap.values() and calls StructureBoundingBox.intersectsWith (offsets 26-90) with no world check. GenStructure and NBTStructure.Start (L1025+) override none of this.
  - Fix: Keep one GenStructure per dimension (Map<Integer, GenStructure>, created on first use for world.provider.dimensionId and removed on that dimension's WorldEvent.Unload), and return early from onLoad on the client. Land it with B-227's per-dimension flag, which touches the same fields.
  - Note: Not yet reproduced in game. To reproduce: load a planet and let a planet structure (for example mun_base) generate, then generate overworld chunks at the same chunk coordinates without a restart. The direct reverse (an overworld start built into a planet) is masked today by B-227, because generate() returns early once a vanilla-generator dimension has populated since the last WorldEvent.Load; it still happens through a saved NBTStructures.dat, and two planets explored at overlapping coordinates share starts both ways. Existing NBTStructures.dat files may already hold foreign starts; they only affect chunks that are still ungenerated.
  - Plan: decision D23
  - Status: open

### Networking, packets, utilities, wiaj (`net-util`)

- **B-265** · gameplay · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/packet/toserver/KeybindPacket.java:42`
  - KeybindPacket.Handler indexes EnumKeybind.values() with an unchecked client int. A client that sends key < 0 or key >= EnumKeybind.values().length gets an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in the handler, which runs on the server main thread (FMLProxyPacket does not override hasPriority, so NetworkManager queues the packet for processReceivedPackets). FMLProxyPacket.processPacket logs it and calls rejectHandshake, which disconnects only that client; the server keeps running. A stock client always sends a valid ordinal (L20) and FML requires the same mod version (@Mod at MainRegistry.java:109 sets no acceptableRemoteVersions), so only a modified client reaches this: a robustness issue, not a crash. AuxButtonPacket.java:89 (`PartSize.values()[m.value]`, see B-282) has the same unchecked pattern server-side; HbmAnimationPacket L83 has it client-side inside a swallowing catch.
  - Evidence: `HbmKeybindsServer.onPressedServer(p, EnumKeybind.values()[m.key], m.pressed);` (registered Side.SERVER, PacketDispatcher.java:43). javap: NetworkDispatcher.handleServerSideCustomPacket fires an FMLProxyPacket down the pipeline and NetworkManager.channelRead0 queues it; SimpleChannelHandlerWrapper.exceptionCaught logs and re-fires, Netty 4.0.10 EmbeddedChannel.writeInbound rethrows through checkException(), and FMLProxyPacket.processPacket catches Throwable, logs 'There was a critical exception handling a packet on channel %s' and calls rejectHandshake (S40PacketDisconnect to that client). EnumUtil.java:7 is `index = Math.abs(index % values.length);`.
  - Fix: `EnumKeybind[] v = EnumKeybind.values(); if(m.key < 0 || m.key >= v.length) return null;` before the lookup. Do not use EnumUtil.grabEnumSafely: it wraps the index with modulo and would turn an invalid packet into a real keybind instead of dropping it. Apply the same bounds check to AuxButtonPacket.java:89 (`m.value >= 0 && m.value < PartSize.values().length`, also listed under B-282).
  - Plan: Phase 6

- **B-267** · crash · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/util/BufferUtil.java:104,114-118`

Compressed NBT of 32768-65534 bytes decodes as a negative length and throws NegativeArraySizeException; exactly 65535 aliases the -1 null marker (empty compound, payload left unread); longer data wraps modulo 65536 into either a positive truncated length (the GZIP IOException is caught at L122, giving an empty compound) or a negative length again. Realistic trigger: ContainerPneumoStorageAccess delta batches of up to 48 full item NBTs in one ContainerNBTCommsPacket (DELTAS_PER_MSG L85, pushNewItem L96-102, bonVoyage L129-133). HeldItemNBTPacket is never sent (its only sender, ModEventHandler.java:1509-1512, is commented out). All 11 BufferUtil.writeNBT/writeItemStack call sites are network serialize/toBytes paths; none is a save.

- **B-408** · leak / perf · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/main/NetworkHandler.java:66`
  - PrecompilingNetworkCodec pads every NTM packet with zeros to at least 256 bytes. encode copies the payload into `Unpooled.buffer()` (initial capacity 256; Netty 4.0.10 grows a buffer by doubling from 64, so below 4 MiB the backing array is max(256, next power of two >= size)), and FMLProxyPacket.toS3FPacket/toC17Packet send `payload.array()`, the whole backing array, which S3FPacketCustomPayload.writePacketData writes in full. Every NTM packet on the wire therefore carries trailing zeros: a 20-byte TE sync costs 256 bytes, a 300-byte one 512. Decoders ignore the tail, but it lets reads past the written data return zeros instead of failing (B-275, the PermaSync CBT_War projectile tail, and B-066, whose client-side readInt of the skipped function ordinal (TileEntityRBMKControlAuto.java:117/127) reads 0 from the padding of an about 87-byte sync and silently sets LINEAR), and it halves the usable size: a client-to-server payload of 16385-32766 bytes is padded to 32768 and fails C17PacketCustomPayload's 32767-byte check, and a server-to-client payload of 1048577-2097050 bytes is padded to 2097152 and fails S3FPacketCustomPayload's 2097050-byte check. That IllegalArgumentException is thrown in NetworkDispatcher.write, and NetworkManager's FIRE_EXCEPTION_ON_FAILURE listener turns it into a disconnect ('Internal Exception'). The main cost today is bandwidth.
  - Evidence: `FMLProxyPacket proxy = new FMLProxyPacket(Unpooled.buffer().writeBytes(outboundBuf), ctx.channel().attr(NetworkRegistry.FML_CHANNEL).get());`. Forge: FMLProxyPacket.java:118-126 `new C17PacketCustomPayload(channel, payload.array())` / `new S3FPacketCustomPayload(channel, payload.array())`; NetworkDispatcher.java:434-436 converts every outbound FMLProxyPacket. Netty 4.0.10: AbstractByteBufAllocator.java:25 `DEFAULT_INITIAL_CAPACITY = 256`; AbstractByteBuf.calculateNewCapacity doubles from 64 (L284-310).
  - Fix: Build the proxy payload on an exact-size array: `Unpooled.buffer(outboundBuf.readableBytes()).writeBytes(outboundBuf)` (an UnpooledHeapByteBuf allocates exactly initialCapacity bytes). Do not use `outboundBuf.copy()` or `Unpooled.copiedBuffer(outboundBuf)`: both go through the pooled buffer's copy(), which allocates from PooledByteBufAllocator, and array() of a pooled buffer is the whole arena chunk, so toS3FPacket would ship the chunk. After the change, reads past the written data throw IndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning zeros; fix the PermaSync CBT_War tail and B-066 in the same batch (after the change, BufPacket.Handler logs a WARN on every such sync).
  - Note: In the owner's pack hodgepodge (increasePacketSizeLimit=true, packetSizeLimit=268435456; found 2026-09-26) raises the S3F limit to 256 MiB, so the server-to-client failure band does not occur there; the zero padding, the zero reads past the end that mask B-066 and the PermaSync tail, and the 16385-32766-byte client-to-server C17 failure remain, so keep the exact-size fix and test the C17 path (for example with a large NBTControlPacket). hodgepodge's codec fix patches only FMLIndexedMessageToMessageCodec.encode, which NetworkHandler's PrecompilingNetworkCodec does not extend.
  - Plan: Phase 5
  - Status: open

A projectile launched or destroyed on the server between CBT ticks makes the lists differ for up to 4 ticks: client projectiles get another projectile's flashtime/travel, or the reader runs past the written data into the payload's zero padding (NetworkHandler.java:66 entry) or past its end, and that exception is swallowed by PermaSyncPacket.java:47 (B-269). The tail is the last section, so nothing else is misread today, but any field appended after it would be. Both sides carry TODOs to remove it.

- **B-410** · leak / perf · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/packet/toserver/NBTControlPacket.java:66-99`
  - NBTControlPacket.Handler loads or generates the chunk at any client-supplied coordinates before checking permission. The handler calls p.worldObj.getTileEntity(m.x, m.y, m.z) (L74) unconditionally; the hasPermission check (L85) comes after. On a WorldServer getTileEntity goes through getChunkFromChunkCoords, and ChunkProviderServer.provideChunk loads, or generates and populates, a missing chunk. A modified client can therefore make the server load or generate chunks anywhere in its current dimension, as fast as it sends packets. The legitimate senders (GUIs, the structure/jigsaw wands, TileEntityTransporterBase.java:402) all address a tile the player is using. AuxButtonPacket has the same pattern (B-282).
  - Evidence: `TileEntity te = p.worldObj.getTileEntity(m.x, m.y, m.z);` (L74) before `if(tile.hasPermission(p)) {` (L85). javap forgeBin: World.getTileEntity(III) calls getChunkFromChunkCoords (offset 114); ChunkProviderServer.provideChunk calls loadChunk when the chunk is not in loadedChunkHashMap and loadChunkOnProvideRequest is set (offsets 1-47).
  - Fix: Move the lookup into the try block and return early when `!p.worldObj.blockExists(m.x, m.y, m.z)` (blockExists only asks chunkExists); the finally block still releases m.buffer.
  - Plan: Phase 6
  - Status: open
- **B-411** · dead code · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/main/NetworkHandler.java:31,124-127`
  - NetworkHandler.flush() and the 'doesn't flush immediately' premise are vestigial. The class comment says this wrapper, unlike SimpleNetworkWrapper, does not flush packets immediately (L31), and ModEventHandler flushes 'ALL network packets' at the end of each server tick (ModEventHandler.java:1573-1579). But every send goes through FMLOutboundHandler.write, which for the PLAYER, ALLAROUNDPOINT, DIMENSION, ALL and TOSERVER targets hands the packet to NetworkDispatcher.sendProxy and on to NetworkManager.scheduleOutboundPacket, which writes and flushes it to the connection at once when the channel is open. flush() on the embedded channels (L124-127) has nothing to flush; only OutboundTarget.NOWHERE, which NTM never uses, leaves messages in the embedded channel.
  - Evidence: `// Essentially the SimpleNetworkWrapper from FML but doesn't flush the packets immediately.` (L31); `public static void flush() { clientChannel.flush(); serverChannel.flush(); }` (L124-127). FML sources: FMLOutboundHandler.java:240-286 (dispatchers == null only for NOWHERE, L30-41), NetworkDispatcher.sendProxy -> manager.func_150725_a (L363-366); javap forgeBin NetworkManager.scheduleOutboundPacket: if channel.isOpen, flushOutboundQueue and dispatchPacket (offsets 11-26); dispatchPacket calls Channel.writeAndFlush (offset 107) or EventLoop.execute (offset 152).
  - Fix: Remove flush() and its call at ModEventHandler.java:1578 and correct the class comment; behaviour does not change.
  - Note: clientChannel, serverChannel and packetCodec are static but assigned in the constructor (L97-107), so a second NetworkHandler (for example a fork-owned channel) would silently redirect every later send and registerMessage of the first instance to the new channel. Make them instance fields before adding a second channel.
  - Plan: Phase 7
  - Status: open
- **B-412** · gameplay · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/packet/toserver/AnvilCraftPacket.java:22-25,43-68`
  - AnvilCraftPacket names the recipe by its index in the client's list, so differing anvil lists craft the wrong recipe. GUIAnvil sends the index of the chosen recipe in the client's AnvilRecipes list (L22-25, GUIAnvil.java:213), and the server crafts `AnvilRecipes.getConstruction().get(m.recipeIndex)` from its own list (L53) after checking only the index range, the open container and the anvil tier. The lists differ whenever one side loads a config/hbmRecipes/hbmAnvil.json and the other does not: GeneralConfig.enableServerRecipeSync defaults to false (GeneralConfig.java:39,101), a syncing server sends only the files it has (ModEventHandler.java:246-265), and a client otherwise uses its own local JSON or the defaults (SerializableRecipe.java:111-160). The server then consumes the inputs of, and gives the output of, a different recipe than the one the player clicked, or does nothing if the player lacks that recipe's inputs.
  - Evidence: `this.recipeIndex = AnvilRecipes.getConstruction().indexOf(recipe);` (L23); `AnvilConstructionRecipe recipe = AnvilRecipes.getConstruction().get(m.recipeIndex);` (L53); `if(InventoryUtil.doesPlayerHaveAStacks(p, recipe.input, true)) { InventoryUtil.giveChanceStacksToPlayer(p, recipe.output);` (L62-63); `public static boolean enableServerRecipeSync = false;` (GeneralConfig.java:39).
  - Fix: Send a fingerprint of the recipe with the index (for example item id, meta and stack size of each output and the input count) and have the server check it against the recipe at that index, falling back to a search of its list and dropping the packet when nothing matches. No change when both lists agree.
  - Note: The fork's DBSRecipes anvil additions run only when no hbmAnvil.json exists (B-148), so a JSON on one side also changes the list length.
  - Plan: Phase 6
  - Status: open
- **B-418** · gameplay · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/packet/toclient/BiomeSyncPacket.java:112-115`
  - BiomeSyncPacket's EndlessIDs branch copies only 255 of the 256 biome entries. When endlessids is loaded, Handler.onMessage copies a full-chunk update into the chunk's short biome array with `for(int i = 0; i < 255; ++i)` (L112), while toBytes/fromBytes carry 256 shorts (L62, L79) and the vanilla branch loops to 256 (L123). Index 255, the x=15, z=15 column of the chunk, therefore keeps its old biome on the client until the chunk is resent: wrong grass, foliage and water colour and a wrong F3 biome there, while the server data is correct. The full-array path is taken whenever fallout rain changes a chunk's biomes (EntityFalloutRain.java:78 and :99 through WorldUtil.syncBiomeChange, WorldUtil.java:54-61; crater biomes are on by default, 17.B_toggle). Both full-array branches also call markBlockRangeForRenderUpdate for the whole chunk inside the loop (L114, L125), 255 or 256 times per packet.
  - Evidence: `for(int i = 0; i < 255; ++i) { target[i] = m.biomeArray[i]; world.markBlockRangeForRenderUpdate(...); }` (L112-115) against `for(int i = 0; i < 256; i++) {` (L123); WorldUtil.java:56-57 sends the full `getBiomeShortArray(chunk)` on the EndlessIDs path. javap of the jar in the owner's pack: `sipush 255; if_icmpge` in the short-array branch, `sipush 256` in the byte branch.
  - Fix: Loop to 256 (or target.length) and call markBlockRangeForRenderUpdate once after the loop, in both full-array branches.
  - Note: Visible only with EndlessIDs installed (the short-array branch); found in the owner's pack (EndlessIDs 1.7.4, crater biomes on) on 2026-09-26. Client-side and visual only.
  - Plan: Phase 6
  - Status: open

The "Using in your project" section (README.md:33-51) is HbmMods text (214b3ef20, MartinTheDragon, 'Configure maven publishing') that points at maven.ntmr.dev and `com.hbm:HBM-NTM:1.0.27_X${ntmBuildNumber}:dev`/`:src` (L48-49), HBM's own artifacts, which carry no suffix and are correct for HbmMods. NTM: Space deliberately appends `_H261` (build.gradle:35, 47614cbcc, George Paton 2024-09-19, '... add space fork identifier to version'), and neither JameH2's branch nor this fork publishes any maven artifact, so under the "NTM: Space" README title the section advertises upstream NTM rather than anything this repository builds.
  - Evidence: README.md:48 `implementation "com.hbm:HBM-NTM:1.0.27_X${ntmBuildNumber}:dev"`; build.gradle:35 `version_name = mod_version + "_X" + mod_build_number + "_H261"` feeds the jar version (L36), the mcmod.info expand (L132), the CurseForge displayName (L187) and the maven version (L212); publishing runs only when `maven.properties` exists (build.gradle:29, 207), which is gitignored (.gitignore:31) and absent, and it targets HBM's credentialed repository (build.gradle:225-236); CI only runs `./gradlew build` (.github/workflows/build.yml:57).
  - Fix: README only: either state that the coordinates pull upstream HBM NTM and that no maven artifact exists for NTM: Space/DBS, or delete the section. Keep the `_H261` suffix: dropping it would make DBS jar names and version strings identical to HBM releases with the same build number.

- **B-287** · silent misconfig · needs a decision · `gradle.properties:19-87`
  - gradle.properties credits has mojibake and punctuation errors. The `credits` value (gradle.properties:5-87) is expanded into mcmod.info (build.gradle:131-133) and shown verbatim in the mod list; it has six problems: L19 holds the UTF-8 bytes EF BF BD (U+FFFD) where 'æ' belongs ('Vær'), L26 has a doubled paren 'Doctor17 (russian localization)),', L44 (Maksymisio) and L73 (SuperCraftAlex) lack the comma before the continuation backslash, mikkerlo is listed twice (L71, L82), and the last line L87 ends in ',\' so the string ends with a trailing comma (Properties.load drops a continuation backslash at EOF). Gradle 4.4.1 reads gradle.properties as ISO-8859-1 while expand and FML use the platform charset, so a build and client with the same charset show 'Vï¿½r' (U+00EF U+00BF U+00BD), not 'V?r'. The bytes came from e20427516 (George Paton 2024-08-07, 'localization, credits, machine usage info'), a Space commit whose parent has the Latin-1 byte 0xE6; HbmMods (9a2eb731a) still has 0xE6.
  - Evidence: `cat -A gradle.properties`: L19 `\ V` + EF BF BD + `r (gas centrifuges, ...`; L26 `\ Doctor17 (russian localization)),\`; L44 `\ Maksymisio (polish localization)\`; L73 `\ SuperCraftAlex (tooltips)\`; L87 `\ impbk2002 (project settings),\` is the last line (wc -l = 87). javap gradle-base-services-4.4.1 `GUtil.loadProperties(InputStream)` calls `Properties.load(InputStream)` (ISO-8859-1); javap forgeBin `cpw.mods.fml.common.MetadataCollection.from` reads mcmod.info with `new InputStreamReader(InputStream)` (platform default) and parses it with Gson; build.gradle sets no filteringCharset for the expand.
  - Fix: Write L19 as `V\\u00e6r` (two backslashes in the file): Properties.load leaves the JSON escape `\u00e6` in mcmod.info, which Gson decodes to 'æ' whatever the platform charset; plain ASCII 'Vaer' also works. Never type a raw UTF-8 'æ': it would show as 'Ã¦' (de8b888f3 'Fix credits' wrote exactly those bytes). Also drop the extra ')' at L26, add the commas at L44 and L73, remove the trailing comma at L87, and optionally merge the two mikkerlo lines. Editing gradle.properties is allowed; the only cost is a possible merge conflict when upstream edits the credits.
  - Plan: decision D4
  - Status: open

- **B-308** · silent misconfig · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/turret/TileEntityTurretBaseArtillery.java:84-88`
  - TurretBaseArtillery.getCurrentTarget returns Java's exception text when the target queue is empty. The direct callback (L84-88) calls targetQueue.get(0) three times without an isEmpty check. With no queued target ArrayList.get throws IndexOutOfBoundsException with a message ("Index: 0, Size: 0" on Java 8, "Index 0 out of bounds for length 0" on JDK 9+); OC maps any non-IllegalArgumentException that has a message to (true, nil, msg) (GTNH OC NativeLuaArchitecture.scala:82-90) and logs nothing by default (debug.logCallbackErrors=false, application.conf:1531), so the script gets nil plus the Java text: no Lua error and no crash, only an unhelpful message. TurretArty's invoke() (TileEntityTurretArty.java:517-518) ends the same way. Because the callback is direct it runs on the OC worker thread while the server tick reads, removes from and clears the same ArrayList, so even a check-then-get stays racy; under that race get(0) can return a slot just nulled by remove(0) or clear(), giving a message-less NPE (WARN stack trace, "unknown error"), still not a crash.
  - Evidence: `return new Object[] {targetQueue.get(0).xCoord, targetQueue.get(0).yCoord, targetQueue.get(0).zCoord};`. Server-thread mutations: TileEntityTurretArty.java:253-257, 292, 376-377, 396; TileEntityTurretHIMARS.java:153-157, 224, 307-308, 343.
  - Fix: `if(targetQueue.isEmpty()) return new Object[] {null, "no target"}; Vec3 t = targetQueue.get(0); if(t == null) return new Object[] {null, "no target"}; return new Object[] {t.xCoord, t.yCoord, t.zCoord};` (one read instead of three get(0) calls).
  - Plan: Phase 4
  - Status: open
- **B-309** · crash · needs a decision · `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/bomb/TileEntityLaunchPadBase.java:522-567`
  - methods()-listed callbacks run as direct PeripheralCallbacks; OC launches spawn entities off the server thread. OC Callbacks.dynamicAnalyze registers every methods() name as a PeripheralCallback before reflection runs and shouldAdd then skips the reflected @Callback of that name (Callbacks.scala:24,44,60-65); PeripheralAnnotation hard-codes direct=true, limit=100, doc="", so in the 32 classes that declare their own methods() list (and through TileEntityProxyCombo, which forwards its core's list, TileEntityProxyCombo.java:536-550) every listed callback runs synchronously on an OC executor thread (Machine.scala:390-393, 968, 1136) whatever its @Callback says. Live today: LaunchPadBase.launch (L522-529, a plain @Callback listed at L545) -> sendCommandPosition (L431-432) -> launchToCoordinate (L419-427) -> finalizeLaunch (L360-374) runs worldObj.spawnEntityInWorld, TrackerUtil.setTrackingRange, the power/tank changes and decrStackSize off-thread; spawnEntityInWorld adds to the chunk, loadedEntityList and EntityTracker.trackedEntities (a HashSet the server thread iterates every tick), so an OC launch can cause an intermittent ConcurrentModificationException or server crash. TileEntityLaunchPadRocket.launch is itself `@Callback(direct = true, limit = 4)` (L616-623, also listed at L648) and calls launch(null) -> spawnEntityInWorld (L271-272), so it races on every path and taking it out of methods() would not help. TurretArty.addCoords (L460-468, listed at L487) runs targetQueue.add on the OC thread while the server tick reads, removes from and clears the ArrayList. The LaunchTable callbacks (setCoords/launch, L676-712) are latent until B-321: the launch table is not an OC component today and has no ports (LaunchTable.java:33-35).
  - Evidence: `@Callback public Object[] launch(...)` at L522-524 is also listed in methods() at L539-547 and dispatched through invoke() (L562-563). javap forgeBin: World.spawnEntityInWorld calls Chunk.addEntity and loadedEntityList.add, posts EntityJoinWorldEvent and calls onEntityAdded; WorldServer.onEntityAdded -> World.onEntityAdded -> WorldManager.onEntityCreate -> EntityTracker.addEntityToTracker (trackedEntities.add); EntityTracker.updateTrackedEntities walks trackedEntities with an iterator. A scan of the 32 classes with their own methods() list finds only these non-direct callbacks promoted to direct: LaunchPadBase.launch, the 6 LaunchTable callbacks and TurretArty.addCoords.
  - Fix: Run the world-mutating OC calls (LaunchPadBase.launch, LaunchPadRocket.launch, TurretArty/HIMARS addCoords, LaunchTable setCoords/launch once B-321 lands) on the server thread. Option A keeps return values: start each with `if(FMLCommonHandler.instance().getEffectiveSide() != Side.SERVER) throw new LimitReachedException();` (li.cil.oc.api.machine, present in the API jar); NativeLuaArchitecture.invoke returns 0 for it (:76-77) and machine.lua (:1087-1100) retries through the synchronized path on the server thread, where consumeCallBudget is skipped (Machine.scala:286-294); getEffectiveSide returns SERVER only on the thread named "Server thread" (javap). Option B: push the call onto a ConcurrentLinkedQueue drained in updateEntity and return {true, "queued"}. Fallback: keep them out of methods() and make LaunchPadRocket.launch non-direct, accepting that ProxyCombo ports (which forward only methods()/invoke(), TileEntityProxyCombo.java:536-550) lose these calls.
  - Note: D27's current recommendation (document B-309) does not fit a server-crash race; the row needs a fix decision. Port reachability (LaunchPad.java:31 and LaunchPadLarge.java:28 create ProxyCombo ports) depends on whether ports are OC components at all (B-319, unverified in-game).
  - Plan: Phase 4 after D27
  - Status: open

- **B-328** · gameplay · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/network/TileEntityRadioTorchBase.java:144-155`
  - setCustomMapValues ignores string values on the LuaJ architecture. On native Lua, args.checkTable returns a live JNLua table proxy (DefaultConverter's AbstractTableMap): containsKey(Integer 1) pushes the key into Lua and finds key 1, and string values arrive as String, so the call works. On LuaJ, OC builds a Scala immutable Map with Double keys and byte[] string values (ScalaClosure.scala:71-80), wrapped by WrapAsJava in ArgumentsImpl.checkTable; containsKey(1) still matches through Scala's numeric equality, but values.get(i) is a byte[], so the `instanceof String` check at L149 fails and no mapping is ever set. The Integer-versus-Double key mismatch the entry used to describe happens on neither architecture.
  - Evidence: `Map values = args.checkTable(0); for (int i = 1; i <= 16; i++){ if (values.containsKey(i) && values.get(i) instanceof String){`; scratch test against scala-library 2.11.5 (Map1, Map3, HashTrieMap): containsKey(Integer 1) = true, get(1) is byte[]
  - Fix: Iterate values.entrySet(); take keys that are instanceof Number with intValue in 1..16; accept String values and byte[] values decoded with new String((byte[]) v, StandardCharsets.UTF_8). This covers live proxies, Scala wrappers and plain HashMaps with Double keys.
  - Note: OC-LuaJIT's marshalling was verified on 2026-09-26. LuaJITArchitecture extends OC's NativeLuaArchitecture and overrides only factory, initialize, save and load, and LuaStateLuaJIT has no behavioural overrides. Component arguments therefore go through GTNH OC 1.12.62's ExtendedLuaState.toSimpleJavaObject (tables become a JNLua DefaultConverter map) exactly as on native 5.2/5.3, and setCustomMapValues works there. The LuaJ failure is still reachable in the owner's pack, which has registerLuaJArchitecture=true.
  - Plan: Phase 4
  - Status: open

The reflective walk still runs lazily once per OC node, the first time it is used (Component.scala:25 `private lazy val callbacks`, read by methods/annotation/invoke at L102-117), and again on each Lua component.methods(address) or component.doc(address, name) call (luac ComponentAPI.scala:58, 85; luaj ComponentAPI.scala:50, 73 -> Machine.methods(component.host), Machine.scala:380), for example each OpenOS component.proxy() build; it does not run on ordinary component invocations, so the cost is negligible. - **B-416** · save data · fix in the fork · `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/network/TileEntityRadioTorchBase.java:122-155`
  - Radio torch OC setters change saved state without markDirty. setChannel, setPolling, setCustomMap and setCustomMapValues (L122-155) write channel/polling/customMap/mapping, which writeToNBT persists (L59-67), but never mark the chunk modified; the GUI path receiveControl does (L113). The sender and receiver call markDirty only when their redstone state changes (TileEntityRadioTorchSender.java:23-24, TileEntityRadioTorchReceiver.java:54-58). The shutdown save (MinecraftServer.stopServer -> saveAllWorlds -> WorldServer.saveAllChunks(true) -> ChunkProviderServer.saveChunks(true)) writes only chunks for which Chunk.needsSaving(true) is true (isModified, or hasEntities with a new world time), whereas a chunk unload saves unconditionally; an OC-made change in a chunk that nothing else marked modified and that holds no entities (Chunk.hasEntities false: none loaded with it or added since its last save) is therefore lost when the server stops before the chunk unloads.
  - Evidence: `channel = args.checkString(0); return new Object[] {};` (setChannel, L124-127; none of the four setters calls markDirty) against `this.markDirty();` at the end of receiveControl (L113)
  - Fix: The four setters are direct callbacks and run on OC's executor thread, so do not call markDirty() in them: TileEntity.markDirty runs World.func_147453_f neighbour updates. Instead, set a volatile dirty flag in each setter; in updateEntity's server branch (L41-44), which both subclasses reach through super.updateEntity() (TileEntityRadioTorchSender.java:36, TileEntityRadioTorchReceiver.java:64), call markChanged() (TileEntityLoadedBase.java:42-44) and clear the flag. Alternative: drop direct = true from the four setters, so OC runs them synchronized on the server thread (the torch lists nothing in methods(), CompatHandler.java:283, so OC honours the annotation), and call markDirty() there; that makes each call take a tick.
  - Note: 41 of 79 setter-like OC callbacks in the tree (set*, move, load, launch) have no markDirty in their body (for example TileEntityBatteryBase setModeLow/setModeHigh/setPriority, TileEntityMachineRadarNT.setSettings); whether those TEs mark their chunk modified elsewhere, such as every tick, was not checked. A fix for any of them must not mark the chunk from a direct callback on OC's executor thread either, see B-309.
  - Plan: Phase 2
  - Status: open

## Reviewed and rejected

Claims from the survey that did not survive re-verification. Do not re-open without new evidence.

- `core` `src/main/java/com/hbm/commands/CommandTotalTime.java:75`: CommandTotalTime.addTime doubles the base time. incrementTotalWorldTime is a setter in 1.7.10 WorldInfo, so add semantics are correct
- `core` `src/main/java/com/hbm/main/ModEventHandler.java:825-831`: WorldEvent.Load re-runs BobmazonOfferFactory.init and the provider override. both calls are idempotent (lists cleared, provider unregistered before re-register)
- `api` `src/main/java/api/hbm/redstoneoverradio/IRORInfo.java:5-6`: IRORInfo PREFIX_*/separator constants are non-final and reassignable. interface fields are implicitly final; the separator constants (`NAME_SEPARATOR`, `PARAM_SEPARATOR`) are in `IRORInteractive.java:7-8`, also an interface
- `te-special` `src/main/java/com/hbm/handler/neutron/NeutronHandler.java:33-47`: RBMKNeutronHandler statics overwritten per world every tick (multi-world race). statics are set per world right before use and not read elsewhere
- `te-special` `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/turret/TileEntityTurretArty.java:325-329`: Arty updateEntity copy decrements casingDelay regardless of usesCasings(). intentional; behaviour equals the base path once cachedCasingConfig is set, no casing spam
- `networks` `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/network/TileEntityPipeBaseNT.java:121-131`: TileEntityPipeBaseNT shadows TileEntityLoadedBase.isLoaded. the subclass overrides isLoaded() consistently; redundant but correct
- `items` `src/main/java/com/hbm/items/ModItems.java:6009`: Survey claim: rbmk_fuel_bk247 unregistered yet feeds craftableRods. registerItem line exists at ModItems.java:6009 (double spaces defeated the survey regex)
- `weapons` `src/main/java/com/hbm/items/weapon/sedna/BulletConfig.java:160-167`: BulletConfig.getDamage gives no flags for PLASMA/MICROWAVE/OTHER. deliberate incomplete switch; missing classes behave like ELECTRIC/LASER
- `weapons` `src/main/java/com/hbm/render/entity/projectile/RenderBulletMK4.java:28`: Survey claim: flamer BulletConfigs get no renderer. null renderer is handled and particles are the intended visual
- `gui` `src/main/java/com/hbm/inventory/container/ContainerRadiobox.java:1`: Survey claim: OrbitalStationComputer/Radiobox containers crash on shift-click. zero slots, path unreachable
- `entities` `src/main/java/com/hbm/entity/cart/EntityMinecartCrate.java:102-104`: EntityMinecartCrate.getCartItem hardcodes EnumCartBase.VANILLA. ItemModMinecart.EnumMinecart.CRATE (L48) only allows EnumCartBase.VANILLA, so getBase() can never differ; the hardcode is equivalent today
- `hazards` `src/main/java/com/hbm/handler/neutron/NeutronHandler.java:34-42`: RBMKNeutronHandler static dial cache races across worlds. the statics are set immediately before that world's runStreamInteractions in the same loop iteration on the server thread and no code outside NeutronHandler/RBMKNeutronHandler reads them
- `hazards` `src/main/java/com/hbm/handler/radiation/ChunkRadiationHandlerPRISM.java:176`: PRISM newAdditions is a static map shared across worlds. putAll/clear happen inside the per-world loop (L183-254) right after that world's spread, single-threaded, so no cross-world mixing occurs
- `render` `src/main/java/com/hbm/main/ClientProxy.java:2188`: AudioDynamic default 10-block range when updateRange forgotten. range is applied by all three proxy overloads; the dropped argument is pitch (separate item)
- `render` `src/main/java/com/hbm/packet/toclient/AuxParticlePacketNT.java:22-23`: Particle creator packets spawn at (0,0,0) when posX omitted. AuxParticlePacketNT(nbt,x,y,z) sets posX/posY/posZ for every IParticleCreator.sendPacket call
- `render` `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/DoorDecl.java:110-111`: DoorDecl.getSEDNARenderer returns client renderers without @SideOnly. interface return type avoids verifier class loading and no server code path calls it
- `net-util` `src/main/java/com/hbm/packet/toclient/BufPacket.java:62`: BufPacket.Handler NPEs on te.getBlockType() in its catch block. te is non-null there and getBlockType() cannot return null for a world-attached tile
- `net-util` `src/main/java/com/hbm/wiaj/cannery/Jars.java:27-28`: Jars.initJars registers CanneryWillow twice. distinct keys for two item forms of the same plant
- `resources-build` `tools/export-json-animation-2_79.py:279-285`: Blender 2.79 exporter will not load on Blender 2.80+. by design: this is the Blender 2.79 variant (`bl_info` blender `(2, 79, 0)` at L11) whose importer uses `object.select = True` (L230, L255) and `scene.cursor_location` (L258-261), both removed in 2.80, and the L279-284 menu guards only pick the menu class; `tools/export-json-animation-3_2.py` and `-4_0.py` are the same script ported to the 2.80+ API (`select_set`, `scene.cursor.location`, annotation-style properties)
- `oc` `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/TileEntityProxyCombo.java:516-535`: ProxyCombo.canConnectNode lacks the ntm_null guard. the ntm_null guard is applied to the core's name on both paths
- `api` `src/main/java/com/hbm/tileentity/machine/TileEntityXenonThruster.java:59-61`: (was B-024) TileEntityXenonThruster sets hasRegistered even when not facing prograde, so a thruster placed at the wrong orientation never retries and never contributes thrust until the tile is recreated. isFacingPrograde (L149-151) reads the core meta, which is written once at placement (`world.setBlock(ox, oy, oz, this, meta, 3)`, BlockDummyable.java:284) and never rotated (MachineXenonThruster implements only ILookOverlay), so a retry cannot change the result; hasRegistered is not saved and is reset on unload (L95-113), and HTR3/HTRF4/HTRNeo/LPW2 use the same deliberate one-shot pattern.
- `blocks-machine` `src/main/java/com/hbm/blocks/machine/BlockMachineBase.java:51-56`: (was B-054) BlockMachineBase.breakBlock skips super when TE is not ISidedInventory, leaving an orphan TE ticking on air. The early return only skips BlockContainer.breakBlock (Block.breakBlock, a no-op for a BlockContainer, plus a redundant World.removeTileEntity); Forge's Chunk.func_150807_a still calls Chunk.removeTileEntity, which invalidates the TE, because TileEntity.shouldRefresh is `isVanilla ? old != new : true` (javap) and only TileEntityFluidValve/TileEntityFluidCounterValve override it.
- `recipes` `src/main/java/com/hbm/config/GeneralConfig.java:47-49`: (was B-139) A user hbmPrecisionAssembly.json silently disables expensive mode. trueExp() (enableExpensiveMode && !PrecAssRecipes.INSTANCE.modified) is only the EXP/328 HUD badge predicate, like true528() and trueRam(): its single caller is RenderScreenOverlay.java:338 (renderBadges), and every expensive-mode switch reads GeneralConfig.enableExpensiveMode directly (GenericRecipe.java:82/84, AnvilRecipes.java:234, ExposureChamberRecipes.java:33, PrecAssRecipes.java:49-138), so a user hbmPrecisionAssembly.json only hides the badge
- `gui` `src/main/java/com/hbm/main/NEIRegistry.java:14-16`: (was B-170) GTNH NEI: handler list built (and memoised) before recipes are initialised, so GTNH NEI shows empty handlers. NEI builds a fresh handler through newInstance() for every recipe or usage query (classic 1.0.3.74 TemplateRecipeHandler.java:455-470; GTNH 2.8.110 likewise), so NEIUniversalHandler's constructor-time recipe copy runs after PostLoad and the init-time prototypes only give IMCSender the class name, getRecipeID() and getMachinesForRecipe(); IMCSender must stay in init (MainRegistry.java:546), because GTNH NEI reads IMC only during FML's IMCEvent, which fires between init and postInit.
- `gui` `src/main/java/com/hbm/handler/imc/IMCHandlerNHNEI.java:42-45`: (was B-171) IMCHandlerNHNEI hard-codes panel size for every handler, so hand-rolled handlers with a different panel (e.g. BreederRecipeHandler's rect at 68,9,30,37) can be mis-sized in GTNH NEI. The 65x166 values equal classic NEI's fixed per-recipe frame (GuiRecipe.java:252,270,289; TemplateRecipeHandler.java:482) and GTNH's HandlerInfo defaults, and every NTM handler draws inside it; BreederRecipeHandler's (68,9,30,37) is a RecipeTransferRect click area (L120), not a panel size.
- `hazards` `src/main/java/com/hbm/handler/ae2/MassStorageMEInventory.java:34-53`: (was B-196) AE2 storage handlers truncate long stack sizes to int, so ME requests above 2^31 items overflow into negative stockpile changes. MassStorageMEInventory is only reached through AE2's MEMonitorIInventory + IMEAdaptor wrapper (MSUExternalStorageHandler.java:36), which narrows sizes to int before calling it (l2i in extractItems, the Integer.MAX_VALUE clamp in getItemStack before AEItemStack.create on inject; javap on AE2 rv3-beta.56-GTNH and rv3-beta-999-GTNH), so the casts at L34/L53 are lossless, and TileEntityMassStorage.changeTotalStockpile ignores non-positive amounts (L169/L185/L208), so no negative stockpile change is possible.
- `hazards` `src/main/java/com/hbm/handler/neutron/NeutronNodeWorld.java:39-43`: (was B-210) NeutronNodeWorld.removeEmptyWorlds drops node caches when a world has no streams, so an idling reactor rebuilds every node next tick. removeEmptyWorlds runs at ServerTickEvent START (NeutronHandler.java:18-28; javap MinecraftServer.tick: onPreServerTick at offset 7, world ticks at offset 58), so a dimension's StreamWorld is dropped only after a whole tick in which no TE there created a stream, i.e. when every reactor is idle, and zero-flux rods and piles already evict their own nodes (TileEntityRBMKRod.java:227-230, TileEntityPileBase.java:35-38); the one-time rebuild is intended memory hygiene (NeutronHandler.java:21-28), WorldEvent.Unload cleanup already exists (ModEventHandler.java:834-837), and keeping worlds with a non-empty nodeCache would retain the never-evicted PILE nodes (B-084)
- `space` `src/main/java/com/hbm/lib/HbmWorldGen.java:88-102`: (was B-224) HbmWorldGen rolls meteorites and crashed spaceships on every celestial dimension, so airless bodies get overworld-style meteor craters and vertibird wrecks with overworld loot at overworld frequencies. Deliberate upstream design: the block is headed '/// CELESTIAL AND EARTH EVENTS' (L87) and came from f0743c3af 'Spawn meteors on other celestial bodies' and 24a511574 'Also spawn crashed spaceships and meteor dungeons!' (George Paton, 2024-06-16), which also added planet surface blocks to Spaceship.GetValidSpawnBlocks (Spaceship.java:32-51); the structure is the legacy crashed Spaceship with POOL_SPACESHIP loot (Spaceship.java:463-493), not a vertibird, so gating it per body is a balance choice, not a fix.
- `net-util` `src/main/java/com/hbm/wiaj/JarScript.java:146,148`: (was B-274) JarScript.ffwTarget/freeRun are static (one fast-forward at a time). Both fields are live only during one synchronous ffw() call on the client thread (JarScript.java:126-143; rewindOne/forwardOne set ffwTarget right before it, and the only callers are GuiWorldInAJar.java:201/209), and nothing outside JarScript reads them, so no other viewer or script can observe or corrupt them; instance fields would be optional cleanup.
- `net-util` `src/main/java/com/hbm/packet/toclient/BufPacket.java:57-67`: (was B-278) BufPacket/EntityBufPacket handlers leak the inbound buffer for non-receivers. On the client the payload is always an UnpooledHeapByteBuf wrapping a byte[] (FMLProxyPacket(S3FPacketCustomPayload) uses Unpooled.wrappedBuffer), which Netty 4.0.10 does not leak-track and the GC reclaims, and the slice passed to fromBytes (NetworkHandler.java:89) is not retained, so the missing release() in BufPacket.java:57-67 and EntityBufPacket.java:49-59 produces no leak and no warning.
- `net-util` `src/main/java/com/hbm/packet/PacketDispatcher.java:76-77`: (was B-281) ContainerNBTCommsPacket is registered twice (discriminators 27 and 28). The packet is dual-direction and NetworkHandler.registerMessage (L109-122) installs the handler on one channel per call, so one registration per side is the intended idiom; 27 is an inbound-only alias because the class-to-byte map keeps 28, discriminators are per-build (never persisted; FML requires the same mod version on both sides) and these are the last registrations, so nothing renumbers. Optional cleanup: pass the same discriminator to both calls.
